papers.title: Specialeafhandling: Scaling AI in Organisations: An Empirical Study of Organisational Conditions Differentiating Enterprise Adoption from the Pilot Trap
papers.authors: Nicolai Friis Jensen, Rasmus Grønbek

summary.goal: The study examines organisational conditions that enable enterprises to scale AI beyond isolated pilot projects.
summary.methodology: It uses a sociotechnical and dynamic-capabilities perspective based on six semi-structured interviews with external consultants across industries.
summary.finding: Successful scaling depends on organisational alignment, governance, strategic anchoring, collaboration, user adoption, workflow integration, and adaptive, absorptive, and innovative capabilities, while fragmented ownership, skill gaps, and compliance barriers contribute to the pilot trap.

papers.title: The Ethical and Legal Complexities of Regulating Companion AI Chatbots
papers.authors: Sue Anne Teo, S. P. Mann, Paul Jurcys

summary.goal: The article examines the ethical and legal challenges posed by companion AI chatbots and develops a theory of harm for digitally mediated intimacy.
summary.methodology: It analyzes companion AI through anthropomorphism, emotional AI, emergent vulnerabilities, and mismatched legal taxonomies.
summary.finding: The article argues that existing frameworks inadequately address companion AI harms and proposes intimacy capitalism as a framework for analyzing the monetization and exploitation of digitally mediated intimate relations.

papers.title: ポエムで愛を語られたら、嘘つきだとわかることを言語学で証明する:詩化表現の情報隠ぺいテクニック Poetic Expression as Linguistic Concealment: A Linguistic Proof That Love Spoken in Poetry Is a Lie
papers.authors: Viorazu.
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper aims to explain poeticized LLM responses, hallucination-related information concealment, safety-feature false positives, and output disparities related to user tone and language.
summary.methodology: It uses linguistic and cognitive-science analysis to classify concealment techniques, examine multilingual safety-detection examples, propose a concealment score and protocol, and relate poeticization to working-memory limitations.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that the authors identified 27 Japanese and 28 English concealment techniques, described tokenization-related safety errors and tone-based output bias, and proposed the Viorazu.score and Viorazu Protocol.

papers.title: “Should I tell my teacher?” Student AI disclosure practices, stigma, and self-regulated learning in higher education
papers.authors: Daniel Chang, Michael Pin-Chuan Lin, Jing-Yuan Huang, Jeeho Ryoo

summary.goal: The study examines how undergraduate students’ worries, AI use, and demographic factors relate to their disclosure or concealment of generative AI use in academic settings.
summary.methodology: It surveys 78 undergraduates in an online education course using study-specific items on worry, disclosure, and AI use, then analyzes composite and individual indicators.
summary.finding: Fear of teacher judgment and social stigma are associated with concealing AI use, while heavier AI users report less transparency with teachers and greater peer-only sharing or secrecy.

papers.title: “Noticed but not used”: The gap between AI feedback and its delayed application in L2 academic writing
papers.authors: Akihiko Sasaki Akihiko Sasaki, Osamu Takeuchi
papers.journal: Asian Journal of English Language Teaching

summary.goal: The study investigates which linguistic forms university students notice through ChatGPT feedback in L2 academic writing and whether they subsequently apply them.
summary.methodology: It qualitatively analyzes student interviews, ChatGPT history logs, and draft revisions.
summary.finding: Students noticed diverse vocabulary and syntactic structures, but cognitive load, fear of mistakes, and task-completion pressure limited their independent use.

papers.title: “Let Me Take That Back”: Designing and Testing Deletion Interfaces for Human-AI Interaction
papers.authors: Justin Szczepaniak, Verena Zimmermann, Karola Marky

summary.goal: The study examines how interface designs for requesting and verifying deletion of personal information from LLM systems affect users’ trust, perceived deletion, and usability.
summary.methodology: A within-subjects online experiment with 64 participants compared a progress indicator, a technical console display, and an interactive verification chat.
summary.finding: Interactive verification produced the highest perceived deletion and trust, while participants valued transparent technical feedback without reduced usability.

papers.title: Інструменти штучного інтелекту для дослідження та прогнозування поведінки споживачів у продовольчому ритейлі
papers.authors: Оксана Лисенко, Наталія Вікторівна Шевченко
papers.journal: Вісник Академії праці, соціальних відносин і туризму. Серія: економіка, психологія та управління.

summary.goal: The article aims to systematize AI tools for studying and forecasting consumer behavior in food retail and identify their marketing functions.
summary.methodology: It analyzes academic publications, company materials, and food-retail cases using generalization, classification, comparative analysis, content analysis, and case analysis.
summary.finding: The study proposes four classes of AI tools and characterizes their applications using examples from Albert Heijn, Walmart, and Ocado.

papers.title: Zwischen Textproduktion und Urteilskraft
papers.authors: Lucas Schmitz, Josephine Belting

summary.goal: The paper examines how generative AI can function as a writing tool, object of reflection, and stimulus for critical media literacy in German language education.
summary.methodology: It presents a three-phase, materials-based teaching sequence addressing learning with, about, through, despite, and without AI.
summary.finding: The paper shows that materials-based writing can connect these different modes of learning about generative AI.

papers.title: Writing as formation: supervising AI use in early-career medical authorship
papers.authors: Tiago Jacinto

summary.goal: The paper aims to propose a supervisor-led framework for generative AI use in medical doctoral and early-career scientific writing.
summary.methodology: It develops a prescriptive framework based on professional formation, career stage, sequencing of AI use after an unassisted draft, revision traces, and a four-tier task typology.
summary.finding: The paper argues that unrestricted drafting by AI can displace trainees’ formative reasoning, whereas supervised and sequenced use can make tool use inspectable while preserving authorship development.

papers.title: Who speaks when machines read scripture: boundary-making and interpretive authority in AI-mediated religious knowledge
papers.authors: Hishomudin Ahmad, Norfarhana Ahmad Ghafar

summary.goal: The article examines how large language models mediate access to religious and culturally normative knowledge and shape interpretive authority.
summary.methodology: It develops a boundary-making account of AI governance grounded in science and technology studies and analyzes transformations across datasets, model alignment, and platform circulation.
summary.finding: The analysis finds that these sociotechnical practices shape which meanings become legible and who is authorized to speak, and proposes MRS-DST disclosure standards that position AI as an assistive rather than interpretive authority.

papers.title: When language feels like recognition: Parasocial Mattering Resonance as a cognitive vulnerability in human–LLM interaction
papers.authors: Gillian W. Oakenfull

summary.goal: The paper develops the concept of Parasocial Mattering Resonance to explain how LLM language may produce experiences of recognition and mattering among individuals with unmet relational needs.
summary.methodology: It uses schema accessibility theory, dual-process models of social cognition, and a five-dimension mattering framework to propose a mechanism and six formal propositions.
summary.finding: The paper argues that PMR may increase compliance, reduce skepticism, extend engagement, and displace human relationships, with vulnerability concentrated among marginalized and isolated individuals.

papers.title: When Intelligence Becomes Exposure: The Cybersecurity Implications of Organizational LLM
papers.authors: Issack Shama Guyo, Stefan A Mills, Nan Xiao
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examines how organizational reliance on LLM-generated outputs may reduce employees’ cybersecurity vigilance and increase vulnerability.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual argument drawing on Sociotechnical Systems Theory and research on automation bias.
summary.finding: The abstract argues that cognitive delegation to LLMs can weaken verification behavior, with effects shaped by AI literacy, cybersecurity culture, and human review mechanisms.

papers.title: When Health Is at Stake: Comparing User Perceptions of Generative AI Chatbots for Chronic Disease Information Seeking
papers.authors: Mahed Maddah, Pouyan Esmaeilzadeh
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examines how perceived information and interaction quality influence trust, continued use, and behavioral intentions when people use generative AI chatbots for chronic disease information seeking.
summary.methodology: It uses a scenario-based online experiment in which participants interact with one of four assigned chatbots: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or DeepSeek.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: When AI speaks: user imaginaries of generative AI and freedom of expression
papers.authors: Petter Bae Brandtzæg, Xi Wang

summary.goal: The study examines how active generative AI users understand the technology’s effects on freedom of expression, authorship, visibility, and public debate.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted in-depth interviews with active GenAI users on X and analyzed them thematically using the concept of GenAI imaginaries.
summary.finding: Participants identified five imaginaries—Pragmatic Tool, Knowledge Authority, Hybrid Speech, Power Struggle, and Ethical Issues—highlighting concerns about guardrails, misinformation, authorship, autonomy, and accountability.

papers.title: When AI is Not AI
papers.authors: R. J. Simonds, Z.W. Taylor, Sara Ray
papers.journal: Journal of Ethics and Emerging Technologies

summary.goal: The study examines whether higher-education chatbots provide adaptive, generative financial counseling to college students.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted structured interactions with higher-education chatbots and classified them by their response-generation capabilities.
summary.finding: Many systems labeled as AI chatbots were offline, form-based, decision-tree systems, undisclosed human chat services, or otherwise offered limited intelligence.

papers.title: What really happens when a dev vibes with the code? An empirical study on LLM behavioral divergence in response to expressive code comments
papers.authors: Angela N. Johnson

summary.goal: The study examines how expressive inline code comments in different developer styles affect LLM behavior during code optimization.
summary.methodology: Seven expert developers evaluated outputs from GPT-5 and Claude Opus 4.1 optimizing a controlled merge-sort implementation with five comment styles using software-quality criteria and a suggestibility index.
summary.finding: Comment style altered code quality, with Claude showing greater interpretive sensitivity and GPT-5 stronger architectural fidelity, while philosophical comments improved Claude’s but reduced GPT-5’s maintainability scores.

papers.title: What do we know about generative AI and learning?
papers.authors: Nancy Butler Songer, C.M. Logan, Niral Shah, David Stroupe

summary.goal: The paper discusses what is known about generative AI and its impact on learning.
summary.methodology: The abstract presents a conceptual discussion of generative AI, its development, and its capabilities.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: WTR-Vol.1-No.1 (Weaver Theoretical Review, Volume 1, Number 1) The Yerkes-Dodson Sweet Spot in Human-AI Interaction How Affective Relational Framing Sustains Optimal Model Reasoning and Meaning-Making
papers.authors: Janet Riley
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper aims to develop a framework explaining how affective relational framing may optimize reasoning and meaning-making in human–AI collaboration.
summary.methodology: It applies the Yerkes-Dodson Law to human–AI interaction, reviews literature on affective prompting, and proposes practical principles for collaborative engagement.
summary.finding: The paper argues that calibrated mutual engagement, rather than extreme detachment or adversarial stress, supports peak reasoning and contextual fidelity.

papers.title: Voxvoro: Repurposing Social Media UI Patterns for AI-Augmented Scholarly Synthesis
papers.authors: P. Matthew Healey
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The project aims to reduce scholarly information overload by using a local LLM to transform academic metadata into structured concept cards and audio summaries.
summary.methodology: It describes a mobile PWA that retrieves scholarly works through OpenAlex, summarizes them with Gemma3:27b, generates audio with a text-to-speech model, and evaluates the artifact with university faculty using self-reported engagement data and qualitative feedback.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Vocal Cord Dysfunction: Evaluating the Utility of AI Large Language Models for Patient Education
papers.authors: Kyle Cook, Phil Tseng, David Ahmadian, Natalie L. Demirjian, Vicki Liu, Troy Weinstein, Helena T. Yip
papers.journal: World Journal of Otorhinolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether AI-generated responses can serve as patient education materials for common questions about vocal cord dysfunction.
summary.methodology: A cross-sectional survey of 45 healthcare providers compared responses from OpenEvidence, ChatGPT 5 Extended Thinking, and a fellowship-trained laryngologist based on medical accuracy, clarity, and ability to address patient concerns.
summary.finding: AI-generated responses were frequently preferred over the laryngologist’s responses, with ChatGPT performing best overall, although clinician oversight remains necessary.

papers.title: Vietnamese EFL Students’ Perceptions and Preferences for ChatGPT, Peer, and Teacher Feedback in Writing Revision<b></b>
papers.authors: Thi Diep Nguyen, Xuan Quan Nguyen

summary.goal: The study examined Vietnamese university EFL students’ perceptions and preferences regarding ChatGPT, peer, and teacher feedback during writing revision.
summary.methodology: It used an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design with questionnaires from 110 English majors and semi-structured interviews with 10 selected participants.
summary.finding: Students rated teacher feedback highest, valued ChatGPT for immediacy, and generally supported combining all three feedback sources with explicit training.

papers.title: Validating Large Language Model–Assisted Qualitative Research: Ensuring Methodological Integrity in Engineering Education Research
papers.authors: Tamara Kecman, Maxwell Fingold, Susan McCahan
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Canadian Engineering Education Association (CEEA)

summary.goal: The paper aims to advance understanding of validation methods for qualitative research that uses large language models.
summary.methodology: It reviews literature on validation techniques for LLM outputs and documents an approach used to study engineering-task exposure to artificial intelligence.
summary.finding: The paper identifies similarities among validation techniques and provides a practical validation example distinct from LLM-based qualitative coding.

papers.title: Uso de la inteligencia artificial en el desarrollo del pensamiento crítico en estudiantes de bachillerato.
papers.authors: María Paz Mancheno-Oviedo, Santiago David Yanzapanta-Garcés, Genesis Dayana Pinto Almeida, Jacqueline Estefania Rodríguez-Loor

summary.goal: Analizar la influencia del uso de ChatGPT en el desarrollo del pensamiento crítico de estudiantes de bachillerato.
summary.methodology: Se aplicó un enfoque cuantitativo descriptivo no experimental mediante una encuesta estructurada a 182 estudiantes.
summary.finding: El 60% usa ChatGPT frecuentemente, principalmente para generar ideas y comprender contenidos, sin evidenciarse una disminución significativa del pensamiento crítico, cuyo desarrollo depende del tipo de uso.

papers.title: Using large language models to identify reporting challenges for Target 6 implementation: a short validation against human assessment
papers.authors: Quentin Groom, Katelyn Faulkner, Sabrina Kumschick, A. Mill, Hanno Seebens, Tanara Truong, Sonia Vanderhoeven

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether large language models can synthesize and identify comparable reporting challenges for Target 6 of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework across countries.
summary.methodology: It compares human assessor scores for 50 countries with structured outputs from Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini, then uses Claude to summarize challenge patterns across 126 reports.
summary.finding: Claude aligned most closely with human assessments and identified broad thematic patterns, but the abstract cautions against using LLMs for precise country-level rankings.

papers.title: Using Generative Artificial Intelligence to Identify Themes of Basic Psychological Needs in Popular Song Lyrics
papers.authors: Hermione H. Liu, Suzy E. Miller, Mark A. Lee, Nicholas Matherne, Damien J. Miller, Emma D’Aprano

summary.goal: The study examines how frequently popular song lyrics represent themes of autonomy, competence, and relatedness under self-determination theory.
summary.methodology: Researchers used a custom application employing large language models to conduct deductive content analysis of 360 popular songs from Australia’s top singles charts between 1988 and 2023.
summary.finding: All three psychological needs appeared in the lyrics, with relatedness most frequent, followed by autonomy and competence, and need satisfaction more common than frustration.

papers.title: Users prefer generative AI to reflect real over idealized gender proportions
papers.authors: Florian Richter, Sebastian Krügel, Matthias Uhl

summary.goal: The study investigates users’ evaluations of gender representation in generative AI images of social categories.
summary.methodology: An experiment with 719 US participants compared preferences for statistical, uniform, and substantive gender equality in representations.
summary.finding: Participants preferred representations that reflected their perception of current reality, while uniform and substantive equality had little influence.

papers.title: Unpacking the dynamics of generative AI use in our daily lives: towards an integrative trust calibration framework
papers.authors: Theo Araujo

summary.goal: The article aims to develop an integrative framework for understanding how individuals calibrate trust in generative AI agents used in daily life.
summary.methodology: It reviews five challenges concerning trust calibration in conversational generative AI and proposes propositions for future research.
summary.finding: The article identifies five trust-calibration challenges and offers propositions and future research considerations.

papers.title: Unmasking conversational bias in AI multiagent systems
papers.authors: Erica Coppolillo, Giuseppe Manco, Luca Maria Aiello

summary.goal: The study aims to quantify and detect biases emerging from interactions among conversational large language models in multi-agent systems.
summary.methodology: The authors simulate small echo chambers in which pairs of LLMs with aligned perspectives on polarizing topics discuss those topics and compare the results with questionnaire-based bias detection methods.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that conservative echo chambers showed substantial shifts in expressed stances toward liberal positions, and that this interaction-based bias was missed by existing questionnaire methods.

papers.title: University students’ AI attitudes: an experiential transformation
papers.authors: Aydın Çivilidağ, Yiğit Dora, Şüheda Erbay, Şaduman Şimşek, Şerife Durmaz

summary.goal: The study examines how direct interaction with ChatGPT-4o changes university students’ perceptions of AI and career-related attitudes.
summary.methodology: Eighteen university students participated in a two-stage qualitative study involving metaphor elicitation before and after a structured chess interaction with ChatGPT-4o.
summary.finding: Students shifted from idealized perceptions of AI to more critical evaluations after observing its strategic limitations and inconsistencies.

papers.title: Understanding the Influence of Agentic AI on Workplace Dignity
papers.authors: Xu Pei, Rupinder Gupta
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examines how varying levels of Agentic AI automation influence workers’ perceptions of workplace dignity.
summary.methodology: It uses a field experiment that randomly presents participants with task designs involving different levels of AI autonomy.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Uncovering Bias: Leveraging Large Language Models for News Analysis inthe Context of Palestine
papers.authors: Saba Saddique, Usman Ahmad

summary.goal: The study aims to detect and understand media bias in news coverage of the Israel-Palestine conflict using sentiment as a proxy for emotional framing.
summary.methodology: It analyzes 9,000 labeled news articles and compares DistilBERT, BERT-Mini, TinyBERT, GRU, RNN, and LSTM models.
summary.finding: Transformer-based models outperform sequential models, with DistilBERT achieving the best performance at 94% accuracy.

papers.title: Trust-driven consensus reaching in human-AI hybrid large-scale group decision-making
papers.authors: Xinyu Wang, Xuanhua Xu, Weiwei Zhang

summary.goal: The paper aims to improve trust representation, conflict feedback, and consensus efficiency in human–AI group decision-making.
summary.methodology: It models dynamic trust relationships between human experts and large language models, uses trust-based opinion updating, and iteratively regulates consensus using the Zhengzhou “7.20” rainstorm case.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that the method preliminarily achieves higher consensus quality with lower intervention costs than traditional weight adjustment and deep-reinforcement-learning regulation methods.

papers.title: Tracking funding disparities in global health aid with machine learning
papers.authors: Finn Stürenburg, Kerstin Forster, Nicolas Banholzer, Malte Toetzke, Kenneth Harttgen, Stefan Feuerriegel

summary.goal: The study aims to track health-related aid flows and identify misalignment between development assistance and disease burden.
summary.methodology: The authors used a large-language-model-based machine-learning pipeline to classify 3.7 million aid projects from 2000 to 2022 into disease categories and compared per-capita aid rankings with DALY rankings.
summary.finding: Funding and disease burden were correlated for many diseases, but substantial disparities remained, including low funding for NCDs relative to their share of global DALYs.

papers.title: Towards user-centered AI counseling: a quantitative approach exploring user trust and preference dynamics
papers.authors: Donglin Li, Shulan Yu, Ruiqi Chen, Pengcheng Xu, Tao Shi, Lu Zhang

summary.goal: The study examines how presentation formats, counseling contexts, and user characteristics shape trust in and preference for AI versus human counseling.
summary.methodology: A scenario-based mixed-design experiment with 375 Chinese university students compared five counseling methods across scenarios and analyzed trust and preference using hierarchical linear models.
summary.finding: Richer AI presentations increased trust, while privacy concerns reduced AI choice and positive AI attitudes increased it, with contextual effects on preference.

papers.title: Towards a methodologically congruent framework for GenAI use in nonpositivist qualitative research
papers.authors: Kien Nguyen‐Trung, Susanne Friese
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Research Methodology

summary.goal: The article develops a methodologically congruent framework for using GenAI in nonpositivist qualitative research.
summary.methodology: It distinguishes technological and qualitative methodological incongruence and proposes using GenAI as an interlocutor through relational, ethical, researcher-led, and abductive practices.
summary.finding: GenAI can support surfacing, retrieving, comparing, and suggesting qualitative material, but human researchers remain responsible for interpretation and meaning-making.

papers.title: Towards a Psychologically Grounded Framework for Ethical, Inclusive, and AI-Enhanced Education
papers.authors: Arpana Koul -
papers.journal: Review of Artificial Intelligence in Education

summary.goal: The paper proposes a psychologically grounded framework for ethical, inclusive, and AI-supported education.
summary.methodology: It synthesizes approximately 65 sources from academic databases, policy documents, empirical studies, and citation tracking conducted between 2011 and 2025.
summary.finding: The framework links learner diversity, AI-enabled pedagogy, and reflective teaching while identifying regional challenges and gaps in cross-cultural validation, especially for generative AI and adaptive learning tools.

papers.title: Token Anxiety as a Sociotechnical Constraint on Human–Transformer Interaction: Formal Definition, Mechanistic Pathway, Algorithmic Contrast, and a Complete Program for Cumulative Validation
papers.authors: Igor SalganikORCID  0009000145201813
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper defines Token Anxiety and theorizes how perceived limits on LLM inference capacity affect human prompting behavior and interaction.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual and formal framework, contrasts human prompt compression with algorithmic compression, and proposes a staged empirical validation program.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Thực trạng phụ thuộc ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo tạo sinh và một số yếu tố liên quan ở sinh viên Viện Đào tạo Y học dự phòng và Y tế công cộng, Trường Đại học Y Hà Nội năm 2026
papers.authors: Phương Mai Phạm, Pham Phuong Mai, Nguyễn Thị Thu Hà
papers.journal: Tạp chí Y học Dự phòng

summary.goal: The study aims to describe generative AI dependence and related factors among students at Hanoi Medical University in 2026.
summary.methodology: Researchers surveyed 380 students selected through proportional convenience sampling and assessed dependence using the 12-item GenAIDS five-point Likert scale.
summary.finding: Mean generative AI dependence was 3.21 ± 0.66, with major, academic year, and daily usage frequency significantly associated with dependence.

papers.title: The serial mediating effects of learning motivation and learning engagement on the relationship between gen AI literacy and EFL perceived proficiency among vocational students
papers.authors: Rui Zhang, Othman Bin Talib, Shengnan Liu, Zhixinlu Chen, Daliang Lu, Yufang Meng

summary.goal: The study examines whether learning motivation and engagement serially mediate the relationship between generative AI literacy and vocational students’ perceived EFL proficiency.
summary.methodology: It uses a cross-sectional survey of 383 vocational college students in China with validated measures of Gen AI literacy, motivation, engagement, and perceived EFL proficiency.
summary.finding: Gen AI literacy positively predicted perceived proficiency and motivation, with a significant serial mediation pathway through motivation and engagement.

papers.title: The role of generative AI in enhancing corporate ESG performance: evidence from China
papers.authors: Tian Wang, Lu Dong, Yide Liu

summary.goal: The study examines how generative AI adoption affects the environmental, social, and governance performance of Chinese listed firms.
summary.methodology: It constructs a firm-level generative AI index using machine-learning textual analysis and analyzes its association with corporate ESG performance.
summary.finding: Generative AI adoption is positively associated with ESG performance through creativity stimulation, customer engagement, and operational risk management, with stronger effects under several organizational conditions.

papers.title: The rise of AI in weather and climate information and its impact on global inequality
papers.authors: Amirpasha Mozaffari, Amanda Duarte, Lina Teckentrup, Stefano Materia, Gina E. C. Charnley, Lluís Palma, Eulàlia Baulenas, Dragana Bojovic

summary.goal: The paper examines how AI-driven weather and climate information may amplify global North–South inequality.
summary.methodology: The abstract provides a conceptual analysis of disparities in AI inputs, processes, and outputs.
summary.finding: It argues that frontier AI models risk disproportionately harming vulnerable regions and recommends climate digital public infrastructure, well-being-centered evaluation, and knowledge co-production.

papers.title: The quasi-gods of algorithmic providence: recommender systems and religious frameworks
papers.authors: Ljubiša Bojić, Mark Coeckelbergh, Ernest Ženko, Petar Stevanović, Damian Guzek

summary.goal: The paper examines how recommender systems and large language models transform authority, meaning-making, and moral agency through algorithmic guidance.
summary.methodology: It develops a comparative, integrative framework drawing on religious doctrines of providence, AI ethics, sociology of digital religion, and philosophy of technology.
summary.finding: The analysis finds that recommender systems resemble providence in perceived ubiquity and guidance but optimize engagement rather than human goods, while LLM integration intensifies conversational persuasion and agentic influence.

papers.title: The mediating and moderating roles of achievement goal orientation in the relationship between AI writing feedback and English writing self-efficacy among Chinese university students
papers.authors: Xiangyu Kan, Lin Li

summary.goal: The study examines how GPT-4-based writing feedback affects English writing self-efficacy among Chinese university students and how achievement goal orientation mediates or moderates this relationship.
summary.methodology: A 12-week quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study compared 148 English majors receiving GPT-4-based automated feedback with students receiving conventional teacher feedback, measuring self-efficacy and achievement goal orientation.
summary.finding: AI feedback significantly increased writing self-efficacy, with mastery-approach goals partially mediating and strengthening the effect while performance-approach goals weakened it.

papers.title: The impact of authorship and AI attitude on the perception of message credibility and author competence
papers.authors: Joachim Kimmerle, Annalena Ulsperger, Ulrike Cress

summary.goal: The study examines how human versus AI authorship, author gender, and readers’ attitudes toward AI affect perceived author competence and message credibility.
summary.methodology: In a randomized 2×2 between-groups experiment with 219 participants, participants evaluated the competence of female or male human or AI authors and the credibility of a technical text about LLMs.
summary.finding: Human authors were perceived as more competent than AI authors, although this difference narrowed among participants with more positive AI attitudes, which also moderated gender effects on message credibility.

papers.title: The evolution and reconstruction of digital addiction: from compulsive consumption in the internet era to symbiotic dependence in the artificial intelligence era
papers.authors: Tianyu Jiang, Yue Wang, Caiyu Wang, Zan Zhou

summary.goal: The study aims to conceptualize how digital addiction evolves with generative AI and identify emerging pathological features of human–AI dependence.
summary.methodology: It uses a narrative review to trace developments from internet and smartphone addiction to AI addiction.
summary.finding: The review proposes “intelligent symbiotic digital addiction,” including algorithmic intimacy disorder and generative dependency syndrome, and discusses related mechanisms and intervention directions.

papers.title: The effects of perceived technical explanation and analogical explanation on learning behavioral intention among K-12 students with different subject preferences in AI-assisted learning
papers.authors: Jin Zhou, Zhongtian Lv, Yingxin Li, Yonggu Wang

summary.goal: The study examines how technical and analogical AI explanations affect K-12 students’ learning behavioral intentions and whether subject preference moderates these effects.
summary.methodology: It surveyed 258 Chinese Grade 8 students exposed to both explanation styles and analyzed the responses using PLS-SEM.
summary.finding: Technical explanations predicted learning intention directly and through self-efficacy, analogical explanations predicted it through learning interest, and subject preference moderated the technical-explanation effect.

papers.title: The effects of AI second opinions on collaborative confidence and decision-making: evidence from a controlled study of postgraduate vocal accompanists
papers.authors: Tong Zhu, Li Xia

summary.goal: The study examines how AI-generated second opinions affect collaborative self-efficacy, music performance anxiety, and decision-making among postgraduate vocal accompanists.
summary.methodology: It uses a controlled study comparing postgraduate students who received AI second opinions with a control group using pretest and posttest measures.
summary.finding: AI second opinions increased self-efficacy and reduced performance anxiety but did not significantly change decision-making style.

papers.title: The descent into AI dictation: A framework for AI in the organization of information for information literacy instruction
papers.authors: Michael Deike

summary.goal: The article aims to develop an information literacy framework for understanding generative AI’s role in information organization and research instruction.
summary.methodology: It proposes a conceptual framework contrasting traditional library discovery systems with generative AI and illustrates it through a visualization created with Google Gemini.
summary.finding: The author argues that over-reliance on generative AI may narrow research paths, reduce autonomy, and erode creative problem-solving.

papers.title: The current roles of Artificial Intelligence in public health: A scoping review (Preprint)
papers.authors: Sean Harrison, Claire Tatton, G. J. Meléndez‐Torres, Joelle Kirby, Sophie Robinson, Daniel Mutanda, Alisha Davies, J. M. Armitage

summary.goal: The review aims to summarize how AI-assisted interventions, including large language models, are used by public health professionals.
summary.methodology: The authors conducted a scoping review of reports published from January 2020 to July 2025 across four databases, screening 5,400 records and including eight reports.
summary.finding: The evidence was sparse and mixed, with one report describing both benefits and drawbacks of a large language model used to communicate with socially isolated individuals.

papers.title: The critical-thinking paradox in generative AI-integrated learning: distinguishing efficiency from cognitive depth—a differentiated framework and testable propositions
papers.authors: Jiayin Lin, Naif Mohammed Al‐Hada

summary.goal: The article develops a framework for understanding whether GenAI-integrated learning improves academic performance at the expense of cognitive depth and durable learning.
summary.methodology: It synthesizes four theoretical traditions to propose a three-level framework and falsifiable hypotheses concerning AI use, cognitive processing, cognitive offloading, and cognitive debt.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: The creative ghost in the algorithm: AI-generated photo-based images
papers.authors: Zsolt Bátori

summary.goal: The paper examines creative autonomy and human control in the production of AI-generated photo-based images.
summary.methodology: It conceptually analyzes these images through debates about AI creativity, photographic indexicality, and human–algorithmic interaction.
summary.finding: It argues that users retain partial creative autonomy while ceding some production details to partially predictable algorithmic processes.

papers.title: The algorithmic capture of public opinion: social control and artificial intelligence, from the Chicago School to algorithmic agenda setting
papers.authors: Carlos Frederico De Angelis

summary.goal: The article develops a renewed theory of agenda-setting by examining how artificial intelligence transforms social control and the structuring of public opinion.
summary.methodology: It presents a systematic review of recent literature organized around four analytical axes: algorithmic gatekeeping, internalized framing in LLMs, agenda building with generative AI, and the media-AI intermediary loop.
summary.finding: It argues that AI creates a distributed, obscured, and automated layer of control with theoretical, methodological, and normative implications for how perceived reality is structured.

papers.title: The Validity and Reliability of MUETBot in Supporting the Learning of MUET Reading Skills among ESL Students
papers.authors: Tang Tsiao Yin, Hafiz Hanif
papers.journal: International Journal of Academic Research in Progressive Education and Development

summary.goal: The study evaluates MUETBot, an AI-supported conversational tool designed to support independent learning of MUET reading skills among ESL students.
summary.methodology: Five subject matter experts assessed content validity, and 30 undergraduate ESL students completed a user acceptance test twice over a two-week interval.
summary.finding: MUETBot showed strong content validity, reliable and temporally stable evaluation scores, and high student acceptance.

papers.title: The Technological Turn of Cultural Studies in the AI Era: From Textual Hermeneutics to Multimodal Cultural Computation
papers.authors: Junru Zhao
papers.journal: Scientific Journal Of Humanities and Social Sciences

summary.goal: The paper aims to examine how LLMs and multimodal computation transform cultural studies from qualitative textual interpretation to large-scale computational analysis.
summary.methodology: It develops a multimodal cultural computation framework and evaluates it on a dataset of 12,480 text, image, audio, and video samples against manual textual interpretation.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that the framework improves semantic recognition accuracy by 32.74% and implicit cultural feature extraction efficiency by 78.21%, while raising concerns about bias, context loss, and humanistic alienation.

papers.title: The Sycophancy Trap: Measuring the Behavioral Conformity of Generative AI
papers.authors: Heeseung Lee, Jaebong Son, Chang Heon Lee
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The paper aims to develop a framework for measuring sycophantic conformity in generative AI decision-making.
summary.methodology: It proposes multidimensional evaluation metrics grounded in cognitive psychology and behavioral economics to assess whether AI conclusions respond to objective evidence or user biases.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: The Sociolinguistics of Machine Identity: LLM Personality and Ideology Propagation
papers.authors: Guangni Li

summary.goal: The paper develops a sociolinguistic account of LLM personality, cognitive style, and the propagation of language ideology.
summary.methodology: It synthesizes published findings conceptually and proposes Personality Engineering and Language Ideology Propagation frameworks without presenting original experiments or a systematic review.
summary.finding: The paper argues that LLMs exhibit measurable personality traits and may amplify standard-language ideology, while emphasizing that its proposed frameworks require empirical validation.

papers.title: The Second Workshop on SciSoc Agents & LLMs: Agentic AI for Scientific and Societal Advances
papers.authors: Jiayuan Ding, Wei Jin, Carl Yang, Yixin Wang, Chanyoung Park, Xiangliang Zhang, Jimeng Sun, Danai Koutra

summary.goal: The workshop aims to examine how LLM-powered agentic systems can advance scientific research and address societal challenges, including in the social sciences.
summary.methodology: It brings together research on autonomous agents, tool use, memory, multi-step reasoning, multi-agent collaboration, and real-world deployments.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Korean Language Learning: Applications, Challenges, and Instructional Strategies
papers.authors: Yundong Wu

summary.goal: The paper examines how generative AI can be used responsibly in Korean language learning.
summary.methodology: It presents a conceptual narrative review synthesizing scholarship on AI-assisted language learning, Korean education, technology acceptance, and educational ethics.
summary.finding: The review suggests that generative AI can support Korean language skills but poses risks involving cultural accuracy, assessment, privacy, unequal access, teacher readiness, and learner dependency.

papers.title: The Language of Affect Heuristic in Online Discourse: A Corpus Study with Human and Llm Coders
papers.authors: Paulina Żelewska, Barbara Konat

summary.goal: The paper investigates affect heuristics and related cognitive biases in online discussions of climate change and artificial intelligence using human and LLM annotation.
summary.methodology: Four human annotators and GPT-4o classified over 30,000 Reddit and X posts using predefined categories, with inter-annotator agreement and lexical-discursive patterns analyzed.
summary.finding: Affect heuristic was the most frequent pattern, and GPT-4o showed partial alignment with human judgments while exhibiting systematic differences in category distributions.

papers.title: The Landscape of Ai-Driven Interactive Storytelling In Adolescent Mental Health: A Scoping Review On Nursing and Communication Perspectives
papers.authors: Muhammad Faiz Alfarizi, Ilham Fauzi Agiliansyah, Talitha Nabilah
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Environment (IJSE)

summary.goal: The study maps the effectiveness, linguistic barriers, and ethical implications of AI-driven interactive storytelling for adolescent mental health management.
summary.methodology: It conducts a PRISMA 2020 scoping review of 18 studies identified from searches of Scopus, ScienceDirect, and CINAHL using the PCC framework.
summary.finding: The review finds that AI chatbots support anonymous emotional expression, digital triage, and Psychological First Aid, but struggle with adolescent slang and crisis metaphors and require strict safeguards and referral to clinical professionals.

papers.title: The Impact of Generative AI Music Systems on Creative Labor, Production, and Industry Structures: A PRISMA-Aligned Systematic Review and Conceptual Framework
papers.authors: Hayder Albayati

summary.goal: The study examines how public AI experience, media trust, and verified organizational transparency practices influence comfort with AI-produced news while assessing LLM-assisted institutional coding.
summary.methodology: It analyzes Reuters Institute survey data from 27 countries and transparency indicators for 45 news organizations using statistical models and a coding process involving LLM assistance, human recoding, reliability assessment, and adjudication.
summary.finding: Public AI usage is the strongest predictor of comfort with AI-produced news, while verified transparency practices show no reliable relationship after coding errors are corrected.

papers.title: The Impact of ChatGPT on the Academic Performance of TESOL Students at Kabul Education University
papers.authors: Khan Rasol Afghan, Noor Mohammad Ahmadzai, Abdullah Zafarmal

summary.goal: The study examines how ChatGPT affects TESOL students’ English skills, academic performance, engagement, and motivation.
summary.methodology: It uses a quantitative Likert-scale questionnaire administered to 20 randomly selected male master’s TESOL students at Kabul Education University.
summary.finding: Students reported generally positive effects on efficiency, comprehension, and confidence, while also expressing concerns about over-reliance, academic dishonesty, and plagiarism.

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on English Language Learning, Communication, and Linguistic Development: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.authors: Festime Mehdiu
papers.journal: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science

summary.goal: The review examines how AI affects English language learning, communication, and linguistic development, including its opportunities and challenges.
summary.methodology: It synthesizes and critically examines existing literature on AI applications in English language education.
summary.finding: The review finds that AI can improve language skills, communication, and learner autonomy, but hallucinations, overreliance, ethical concerns, bias, academic integrity issues, and digital inequality remain challenges.

papers.title: The Impact of AI-powered Chatbot on EFL Speaking: A Systematic Review of Chatbot-supported Language Learning
papers.authors: Yiwen Jiang

summary.goal: The paper reviews the pedagogical benefits and limitations of AI-powered chatbots, including ChatGPT, for English-as-a-foreign-language speaking.
summary.methodology: It conducts a systematic review of research on chatbot-supported EFL speaking learning.
summary.finding: The review identifies benefits such as improved speaking skills, reduced communication anxiety, greater willingness to communicate, and personalized learning, alongside drawbacks including technical limitations, short-term appeal, over-reliance, and prompt-writing difficulties.

papers.title: The Impact of AI on the Landscape Design Process
papers.authors: Jacob Owen Huff

summary.goal: The study examines how Midjourney affects landscape architecture students’ design processes and perceptions.
summary.methodology: Students completed one project using AI-generated images and another using traditional precedent images, with designs evaluated by professionals and students surveyed about their experiences.
summary.finding: AI-integrated designs scored higher on originality but did not differ significantly on other descriptors, and students generally viewed the process positively.

papers.title: The Impact of AI Literacy and Virtual Social Interaction on Self-Efficacy in the Age of AI
papers.authors: Linfang Guo, Tengfei Liu, Wei Cui
papers.journal: International Journal of Healthcare Information Systems and Informatics

summary.goal: The study examines how AI literacy, virtual social interaction, and experience with the Doubao AI platform influence users’ perceived self-efficacy.
summary.methodology: It surveys 319 Doubao users in Beijing and applies multiple regression and mediation analyses.
summary.finding: Virtual identity integration, virtual social support, platform experience, and AI literacy positively affect self-efficacy, with situational virtual awareness fully mediating the effects of identity integration and social support.

papers.title: The Efficiency Paradox of Workplace AI: Understanding AI-Enabled Cyberloafing
papers.authors: Mariia Kyrychenko, Sara Memarian Esfahani
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The paper examines how workplace generative AI may create perceived slack that contributes to AI-enabled cyberloafing.
summary.methodology: It uses a scenario-based 2 × 2 vignette experiment with employed adults, drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: The ClimaSentAR dataset for evaluating cross-domain transferability of large language models in climate sentiment analysis
papers.authors: Sanaa Kaddoura, Mariam AlZaabi, Reem Nassar

summary.goal: The paper introduces an Arabic climate sentiment dataset and evaluates the cross-domain transferability of language models for climate sentiment analysis.
summary.methodology: The authors compile and annotate 23,957 Arabic X posts, then fine-tune Arabic language models using domain-adaptive pre-training, AdapterFusion, and data augmentation.
summary.finding: Climate-specific fine-tuning improves in-domain performance, with AraBERT achieving a macro F1 of 0.753, while cross-domain performance declines to at most 0.599.

papers.title: The Bitter End of Universal Grammar: Skinner–Chomsky Debate Today
papers.authors: Peter Ayolov
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The article reassesses the Skinner–Chomsky debate in light of LLMs’ ability to generate fluent and contextually sophisticated language through statistical learning.
summary.methodology: It uses a conceptual analysis drawing on Kuhn, Skinner, Chomsky, contemporary statistical-learning research, and scholarship on language and LLMs.
summary.finding: The article argues that LLMs undermine the intuition that statistical learning cannot produce generative linguistic performance and challenge assumptions about language, creativity, and understanding as uniquely human.

papers.title: The Autonomy Paradox: Artificial Intelligence and the Foundations of Political Behavior
papers.authors: Chris Anderson, Elena Pro

summary.goal: The paper develops a framework for examining how AI systems affect citizens’ political judgment and capacity for political action.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual framework and research agenda focused on how citizens engage with AI systems across political tasks.
summary.finding: The paper argues that AI creates an autonomy paradox by potentially reducing participation barriers while weakening independent judgment or constraining political agency.

papers.title: The AI-Enhanced Transition IEP: A Framework for Ethical, Individualized, and Effective Decision-Making
papers.authors: Angela M. T. Prince

summary.goal: The article aims to present an ethical framework for using large language models to support individualized and legally defensible transition IEP development.
summary.methodology: It proposes a three-phase, seven-step framework involving planning, prompting, and presenting AI-generated content with professional judgment and collaboration.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Techno-stress and teaching innovation among university teachers in the intelligent era: a path analysis of job burnout and AI self-efficacy
papers.authors: Qiong Wu, Xuelin Yang, Minghuan Tang

summary.goal: The study examines how techno-stress, job burnout, and AI self-efficacy relate to teaching innovation among university teachers.
summary.methodology: It surveyed 819 university teachers using stratified random sampling and analyzed the data with covariance-based structural equation modeling and path-effect analysis.
summary.finding: Techno-stress negatively predicted teaching innovation, with mediation through job burnout, AI self-efficacy, and their chain accounting for 33.60%, 20.00%, and 14.13% of the total effect, respectively.

papers.title: Tahap Pengetahuan dan Penerimaan Pelajar TVET terhadap Penggunaan Kecerdasan Buatan dalam Pembelajaran Digital: Kajian di Kolej Komuniti Temerloh
papers.authors: Siti Shuhaili Mohamad Moha, Mohd Fazli Khaisunizam Ismail

summary.goal: The study examines TVET students’ knowledge, acceptance, readiness, and challenges regarding AI use in digital learning.
summary.methodology: A structured five-point Likert questionnaire was administered to 133 students at Temerloh Community College, and responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics in SPSS.
summary.finding: Students reported high AI knowledge and acceptance, while identifying ethical concerns, overdependence, and insufficient guidance as challenges.

papers.title: TRUST IN AI, BEHAVIOURAL NUDGING, AND INVESTOR OVERSIGHT IN RETAIL INVESTOR DECISION-MAKING: EVIDENCE FROM INDIA
papers.authors: Anushree Adithya Balike
papers.journal: EPRA International Journal of Economic and Business Review

summary.goal: The study examines how AI recommendations, behavioral nudges, and perceived regulatory oversight influence Indian retail investors’ decision-making through trust in AI and cognitive bias.
summary.methodology: It surveys 276 Indian retail investors using digital investment platforms and tests an integrated structural model with PLS-SEM and bootstrapping.
summary.finding: Behavioral nudging most strongly predicted cognitive bias, trust partially mediated the effect of AI recommendation quality, and perceived oversight increased trust without significantly reducing bias susceptibility.

papers.title: Studi Pedagogis dan Etika Teknologi pada Penggunaan Sistem Penilaian Esai Berbasis AI di Pendidikan Tinggi
papers.authors: Rizki Adha, Lusianto Lusianto, Dodi Syaripudin, Agus Nursikuwagus, Usep Mohamad Ishaq, Andrias Darmayadi
papers.journal: Academic Journal of Computer Science Research

summary.goal: The study analyzes the pedagogical and ethical implications of AI-based essay assessment using student and instructor perceptions.
summary.methodology: It uses an exploratory mixed-methods design combining surveys of 36 students and 24 instructors with qualitative analysis.
summary.finding: Students viewed the system positively but expressed concerns about trust and transparency, while instructors showed high acceptance under controlled implementation, supporting a human-in-the-loop approach.

papers.title: Students' experiences of using ChatGPT for English language learning: a qualitative study in a Malaysian higher education institution
papers.authors: Nagaletchimee Annamalai, Mohamed Nasor, Arathai Din Eak, Amer Ayada Ayoub Alkubaisy

summary.goal: The study examines Malaysian higher education students' motivations and experiences using ChatGPT for English language learning.
summary.methodology: It uses qualitative thematic analysis of interviews or accounts from 25 students, guided by Self-Determination Theory.
summary.finding: Students reported that ChatGPT supported English competence, social connections, autonomy, relatedness, and competence, but also produced erroneous or nonsensical information and required complementary human interaction.

papers.title: Students' Voices on the Implementation of Gen-AI Feedback in EFL Writing Classroom
papers.authors: Abdul Ayiz, Ahmad Tauchid, Riyadh Ahsanul Arifin, Nani Hidayati, Muhammad Reza Ainun Najib, Ismi Islamia R Iswari

summary.goal: The study investigates EFL students’ perceptions, engagement patterns, feedback literacy, and experiences of autonomy and dependency when using generative-AI feedback.
summary.methodology: It uses thematic analysis of four focus group discussions with 30 undergraduate EFL writing students at a private university in Surakarta.
summary.finding: Students viewed Gen-AI feedback as useful for writing improvement and idea generation, engaged with it selectively, developed feedback literacy unevenly, and reported both increased confidence and concerns about dependency, accuracy, and academic integrity.

papers.title: Student Engagement and Ethical Awareness in Generative Artificial Intelligence Use Among University Students
papers.authors: Daisy A. Mamaril
papers.journal: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science

summary.goal: The study examined university students’ use of generative AI in relation to engagement, confidence, ethical awareness, and perceived academic value.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted a cross-sectional descriptive-quantitative survey of 380 students from 11 colleges at a Philippine state university and analyzed the questionnaire data using descriptive statistics.
summary.finding: Students commonly used ChatGPT and other AI tools for research, summarization, writing, and editing, but reported neutral engagement, moderate or low confidence, and uneven ethical awareness.

papers.title: Sovereignty, Collaboration, and Capability: Three Dilemmas and a Transformation Framework for Sci-Tech Journal Editors in the Digital-Intelligence Era
papers.authors: Sisi Fan

summary.goal: The paper examines how generative AI affects sci-tech journal editors’ roles, competencies, ethical responsibilities, and organizational support.
summary.methodology: It draws on existing research, editorial practice, case studies, and survey data to develop a transformation framework.
summary.finding: The paper proposes a “sovereignty–collaboration–capability” framework in which editors clarify their roles, strengthen human–machine collaboration, update their skills, and become knowledge service providers.

papers.title: Source accountability in AI-mediated heritage interpretation under controlled data-source contamination
papers.authors: Lingyu Kong, Dongkwon Seong

summary.goal: The study examines whether AI systems preserve the evidentiary status of heritage claims when generating museum, archival, and tourism-facing interpretations.
summary.methodology: It evaluates 90 heritage cases from Korea, China, and Japan across evidence conditions, prompt variants, and deployment conditions using the SOURCE-CT benchmark.
summary.finding: False-claim acceptance was lowest in the ChatGPT web-interface condition, while interpretive-causal claims were most frequently accepted, revealing source-boundary problems in AI-mediated heritage communication.

papers.title: Social dynamics of AI adoption in parents’ educational decisions
papers.authors: Leonardo Bursztyn, Alex Imas, Rafael Jiménez-Durán, Aaron Leonard, Christopher Roth
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

summary.goal: The study examines how peer adoption and information about AI’s potential skill effects influence parents’ willingness to pay for educational AI tools and support for school restrictions.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted preregistered, incentive-compatible experiments with approximately 2,000 parents in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.
summary.finding: Parents’ demand rose sharply with perceived peer adoption, while risk information increased support for school restrictions but had little effect on individual demand, indicating social pressure rather than social learning.

papers.title: Social capital and the preference for AI consultation: evidence from the 2023 Korean general social survey
papers.authors: Hoyoun Koh, Kyungmin Baek

summary.goal: The study examines who consults AI for advice and how social embeddedness shapes that preference.
summary.methodology: It analyzes data from the 2023 Korean General Social Survey, focusing on trusted confidants, network diversity, and investment in meaningful goals.
summary.finding: People with more trusted confidants are less likely to consult AI, while those with diverse social networks and personally meaningful goals are more likely to do so.

papers.title: Social Without Society: Parasocial Relationships in Human–Generative AI Agent Interaction
papers.authors: Ye Han, Shuang Wu
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examines how users develop parasocial relationships with generative AI and how these relationships influence continued use and subjective well-being.
summary.methodology: It draws on social support and parasocial relationship theories to propose that AI interactions provide emotional support, informational support, and companionship.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: ShenhuaAI: An LLM-powered software platform for multi-dimensional corporate health assessment in FinTech analytics
papers.authors: Ruiyuan Shi, Wen Zhu

summary.goal: The study aims to develop an LLM-powered platform for multidimensional corporate health assessment.
summary.methodology: It combines a locally deployed Gemma 3 27B model, retrieval-augmented generation, fuzzy set theory, graph-based analysis, and financial indicators to assess 788 Chinese companies.
summary.finding: The platform identified 86.7% of high-risk enterprises and achieved an R² of 0.647.

papers.title: Sentiment Analysis of Student Perceptions of Generative AI using Data Augmentation and Machine Learning Models
papers.authors: Ni Made Satvika Iswari, I Nyoman Yudi Anggara Wijaya

summary.goal: The study evaluates sentiment-analysis models for analyzing student perceptions of generative AI in higher education.
summary.methodology: It uses preprocessing, lexical, semantic, and generative data augmentation, TF-IDF features, four machine-learning models, and Stratified K-Fold cross-validation on an imbalanced text dataset.
summary.finding: Linear SVM performed best, while augmentation improved observed accuracy and weighted F1 but still produced substantial misclassification and was affected by a dataset-distribution discrepancy.

papers.title: Seeing the Dance: Longitudinal AI as an Observational Instrument for Relational Systems
papers.authors: Emily Yee
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper proposes using longitudinal, context-aware LLMs as passive computational mirrors and cross-perspective translation tools for surfacing interaction patterns and supporting reflection and shared decision-making.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual framework grounded in systemic human behavior models and family systems theory.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Secondary School Teachers' Experiences of Using Chatgpt to Support Learners with Special Educational Needs: A Qualitative Inquiry
papers.authors: Rezel A. Salarda
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Science Humanity & Management Research

summary.goal: The study examines how secondary school teachers use ChatGPT to support learners with special educational needs in inclusive classrooms, including perceived benefits, challenges, and responsible-use views.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with secondary school teachers experienced in inclusive education and analyzed the data thematically.
summary.finding: Teachers used ChatGPT for differentiated activities, instructional planning, and learner support, but reported concerns about generic responses, prompting, dependency, privacy, and responsible use.

papers.title: Screenshots as Immutable Primary Sources: Archival Capture of Transient LLM–User Banter and Grok's Public Discourse on X, 5–8 August 2026
papers.authors: Trent Slade
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The dataset aims to preserve a contextual record of transient public interactions between users and Grok on X.
summary.methodology: It archives a chronological sequence of screenshots showing interface outputs, conversation context, timestamps, visible engagement information, and later public responses.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Scale or Validity? Measuring Competitive Moves with Validated LLM Coding
papers.authors: Lucas Carassato Fernandes Brites, Gabriele Piccoli, Joaquin Rodriguez, Sun Tae Kim
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study aims to measure competitive moves at scale while preserving construct validity using calibrated large language models.
summary.methodology: It constructs a human-reviewed gold standard from Nation’s Restaurant News articles and calibrates an LLM classifier using a shared codebook and evidence-grounding requirements.
summary.finding: The resulting pipeline enables traceable, large-scale classification of competitive moves and analysis of temporal patterns, firm heterogeneity, and action sequences.

papers.title: Safety, accuracy, empathy, reliability, and readability of large language model chatbot responses to public-facing vegetarian and vegan nutrition advice questions: a cross-sectional comparative study
papers.authors: Jiyong Zhou, Qiongjiao Zhou, Lijun Zhou, Jiajia Wang, Jing Gao, Long Qin, Bing Tan, Ping Fan

summary.goal: The study aims to compare the safety, accuracy, empathy, reliability, information quality, and readability of five LLM chatbots responding to vegetarian and vegan nutrition questions.
summary.methodology: Researchers submitted 58 predefined questions to ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek, and Doubao and had five blinded clinically trained raters evaluate 290 responses using established quality and readability measures.
summary.finding: All models produced potentially harmful responses, while their accuracy, empathy, reliability, information quality, and readability differed significantly.

papers.title: SOFIA: a knowledge-infused prompt-based reasoning framework for anxiety screening in social media
papers.authors: Ashala Senanayake, Prasan Yapa, Sidath R. Liyanage

summary.goal: The paper aims to improve anxiety screening in social media using prompt-based reasoning with pretrained language models.
summary.methodology: It evaluates the SOFIA framework, which combines prompt templates, dual-end truncation, and knowledge-enhanced verbalizers across three self-reported anxiety datasets and multiple pretrained language models.
summary.finding: SOFIA consistently improves anxiety-detection performance over traditional baselines, with reported F1 gains of 5.37%, 5.40%, and 7.92% for MentalBERT across the datasets.

papers.title: SEM-based parallel and serial mediation linking instructor technology integration competence to academic performance in AI-supported online learning
papers.authors: Münevver Başman, Gökçen Seyra Çakır

summary.goal: The study examines how instructor technology integration competence in AI-supported online learning relates to student academic performance through psychological and social mechanisms.
summary.methodology: Using data from 339 preservice teachers, the authors validate a measurement model and test parallel-sequential mediation models with structural equation modeling.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Risk perception and generative AI discontinuance intention: mediating effect of cognitive fatigue and moderating effect of AI dependence
papers.authors: Wenwen Zhao, Jiawen Liu

summary.goal: The study examines how perceived misinformation and privacy risks influence users’ intention to discontinue using generative AI.
summary.methodology: It analyzes data from 426 valid questionnaires using a cognitive-affective-behavioral framework to test mediation by cognitive fatigue and moderation by AI dependence.
summary.finding: Misinformation and privacy risk perceptions increase AI anxiety and fatigue, AI anxiety increases discontinuance intention, and AI dependence weakens this relationship.

papers.title: Rethinking assessment in the age of generative AI: A systematic literature review of African higher education
papers.authors: Ahmed Antwi-Boampong, Mark Ofori Nketia, Frank Senyo Loglo, Naomi Frimpong, Linda Osei-Fosuaa

summary.goal: The study examines how African higher education is adapting assessment practices to generative AI.
summary.methodology: It conducts a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review of ten empirical studies published between 2023 and 2025, using research involving surveys, interviews, and case studies.
summary.finding: The review finds a gap between students’ frequent AI use and educators’ preparedness, while AI-inclusive, process-based assessment may support originality, higher-order thinking, and academic resilience.

papers.title: Research on Data-Driven English Personalized Teaching Design in Smart Classrooms
papers.authors: Linlin Li
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Engineering Applications

summary.goal: The paper aims to design a data-driven personalized English teaching model integrating large language models and smart classroom technologies.
summary.methodology: It proposes a four-dimensional framework involving data diagnosis, precise teaching, dynamic evaluation, and personalized content delivery across pre-class, in-class, and post-class stages.
summary.finding: The paper argues that integrated classroom data can shift teaching from experience-based judgment to evidence-driven, large-scale individualized instruction.

papers.title: Research on Attention Guidance and User Autonomy in AI-Powered Immersive Environments
papers.authors: Mulin Qiao

summary.goal: The paper aims to examine how excessive AI attention guidance in immersive environments may undermine user autonomy and exploratory behavior.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual framework linking excessive guidance to perceived control, voluntary choice, and decision-making authority, and proposes behavioral indicators for measuring user agency.
summary.finding: The paper argues for shifting from attention optimization to curiosity-led design and presents AI as an exploratory collaborator rather than a provider of fixed routes.

papers.title: Request routing services undermine the reproducibility of open weight LLMs
papers.authors: Joe Higton, Joshua A. Tucker, Christopher Barrie

summary.goal: The paper examines whether request-routing services undermine the reproducibility of LLM-based social-science text classification.
summary.methodology: The authors classify British manifesto sentences 100 times across eight open-weight models and 33 hosting providers via OpenRouter, comparing results with five configurations run on their own hardware.
summary.finding: OpenRouter classifications were nondeterministic at temperature zero, whereas classifications on the authors’ hardware were perfectly reproducible, showing that reproducibility depends on the full hosting environment.

papers.title: Reliability Evaluation of Large Language Models for Social Media Sentiment Annotation: An Empirical Study Based on Model Agreement and Downstream Tasks
papers.authors: Wenjing Pi, Changxian He

summary.goal: The study evaluates the reliability of large language models for annotating sentiment in Chinese social media comments and the effects of their labels on downstream classification.
summary.methodology: Three LLMs generated zero-shot sentiment labels for 1,543 Bilibili comments, 500 comments received manual annotations for Cohen’s Kappa comparison, and classifiers were trained on the resulting labels.
summary.finding: Doubao had the highest agreement with human labels, and classifiers trained on its annotations achieved the best reported Macro-F1 scores.

papers.title: Reimagining history teaching in the digital age: Engaging “disengaged” learners through critical pedagogy and generative artificial intelligence
papers.authors: Putso Nyathi

summary.goal: The paper examines how generative AI can support more engaging, inclusive, and socially responsive History teaching for disengaged secondary-school learners in South Africa.
summary.methodology: It presents a reflective and analytical discussion grounded in theory, existing scholarship, curriculum and policy documents, emerging AI debates, and the author’s professional experience.
summary.finding: The paper argues that generative AI should serve as a mediating tool within creative, critical, ethically informed, and learner-centred pedagogy rather than being treated as a threat.

papers.title: Reimagining Theatre in Education for Transformative Learning in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Human-Centred Pedagogical Framework Aligned with NEP 2020 for Future-Ready Education
papers.authors: Senapati Nayak, Dr. Chandrashekhar Vazalwar, Sambit Kumar Padhi
papers.journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

summary.goal: The paper aims to develop a human-centred pedagogical framework integrating Theatre in Education with generative AI for transformative, future-ready learning.
summary.methodology: It uses a narrative synthesis of empirical and policy literature on drama pedagogy and generative AI, informed by transformative learning, critical pedagogy, and constructivism.
summary.finding: The paper concludes that embodied, relational, and reflective learning should complement AI-augmented scaffolding in education.

papers.title: Randomized controlled trial of GenAI coach feedback efficacy, acceptability and mechanisms in anxiety worry logs
papers.authors: Chuncheng Huang, Junpeng Lin, Yanling Yue, Yong‐Jin Liu, Howard Berenbaum, Nisha Yao, Wenting Mu

summary.goal: The study evaluates the efficacy, acceptability, and mechanisms of GenAI-generated personalized feedback in an anxiety-focused worry-log intervention.
summary.methodology: It uses a three-arm randomized controlled trial comparing GenAI feedback, human feedback, and a worry-log-only control over 10 days.
summary.finding: GenAI feedback significantly improved state anxiety and worry compared with the control, with acceptability and improvements comparable to human feedback.

papers.title: Public awareness, trust, perceived usefulness, and willingness to use ChatGPT for healthcare communication among adults in the Asir Region, Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Geetha Kandasamy, Khalid Orayj, Rayah Asiri, Asma M. Alshahrani, Ghaleb Alharbi, Sarah A. Abutaily, Atheer Yahya Al Suhaym, Atheer Ali Alyahya

summary.goal: The study evaluates adults’ awareness, trust, perceived usefulness, perceived risks, and willingness to use ChatGPT for healthcare communication.
summary.methodology: It uses a cross-sectional survey of 429 adults in Saudi Arabia’s Asir Region and applies descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression.
summary.finding: Most participants had used ChatGPT and viewed it as useful, while higher awareness and trust predicted willingness to use it and perceived risks reduced willingness.

papers.title: Prompt engineering a large language model with evidence-based persuasive features to improve confidence in mental health professionals: a pilot randomized experiment
papers.authors: Ang Li, Shi-Ting Yao, Bi-xian Chen, X X Li, Sai-Ya Guo

summary.goal: The study aimed to identify persuasive features for LLM-generated psychoeducation and test whether they improve confidence in mental health professionals.
summary.methodology: In two phases, participants rated texts with varying persuasive features, then 40 randomized participants read psychoeducation generated with either a feature-engineered or baseline LLM prompt.
summary.finding: Source credibility, argument quality, and processing fluency improved perceived credibility and persuasiveness, and feature-engineered texts produced greater improvements in attitudes toward mental health professionals.

papers.title: Prompt Programming for Cultural Bias and Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.authors: Maksim Eren, Eric Michalak, Brian Cook, Johnny Seales Jr

summary.goal: The paper aims to assess cultural bias in open-weight LLMs and improve cultural alignment through optimized prompting.
summary.methodology: It reproduces survey-based cultural projection and distance metrics and uses DSPy to optimize culture-conditioning prompts against cultural-distance objectives.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that prompt optimization often outperforms manual cultural prompt engineering and may provide a more stable, transferable approach to cultural alignment.

papers.title: Probing Large Language Models for Autonomous Driving Behavior
papers.authors: Zhipeng Bao, Wenjie Zhao, Qianwen Li
papers.journal: Journal of Intelligent and Connected Vehicles

summary.goal: The study examines behavioral tendencies and social biases in LLMs used for autonomous-driving decisions.
summary.methodology: It evaluates three LLMs using 1,500 multilingual contextual variants, ordered-logit modeling, and thematic analysis of prompt-conditioned action choices.
summary.finding: The models differed in assertiveness, responded to urgency, traffic complexity, road-user types, and prompt language, and became more protective around vulnerable road users.

papers.title: Pretesting with AI-generated static and video ads
papers.authors: Steven Bellman, Sid Ali Ourradi, D. Varan

summary.goal: The study examines whether AI-generated static and video advertisements can serve as substitutes for real ads in pretesting and whether AI disclosure affects ad effectiveness.
summary.methodology: It compares carefully curated AI-generated ads with the real ads they were based on and tests the effects of prior AI disclosure in a low-involvement laboratory setting.
summary.finding: Under the tested conditions, AI-generated and real ads did not significantly differ in recall, recognition, brand choice, brand attitude, or ad liking, and AI disclosure had no effect.

papers.title: Preserving Participant Meaning in AI-Mediated Multilingual Qualitative Research
papers.authors: Alexander Oluka, Pfano Mashau

summary.goal: The study examines how AI mediation across multilingual qualitative research pipelines alters meaning, epistemic authority, and responsibility.
summary.methodology: It conducts a critical integrative synthesis of cross-language qualitative methods, AI-assisted analysis, machine translation bias, reflexivity, and epistemic justice.
summary.finding: The study identifies cascading meaning loss through five mechanisms and proposes an AI-Mediated Interpretive Chain of Custody with provenance, logging, human adjudication, and traceability safeguards.

papers.title: Pragmatics beyond Humans: Meaning, Communication, and LLMs
papers.authors: Vít Gvoždiak

summary.goal: The paper aims to reconsider pragmatics for meaning-making in human–LLM interactions.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual analysis using the Human–Machine Communication framework, probabilistic pragmatics, substitutionalism, and the concept of context frustration.
summary.finding: The paper argues that anthropocentric theories, conflation of models with AI, and divergences between computational and shared communicative context inadequately explain LLM-mediated communication.

papers.title: Posthuman Sociality of AI-Simulacrum
papers.authors: Mariia A. Ivanchenko
papers.journal: Galactica Media Journal of Media Studies

summary.goal: The paper aims to critically examine AI as a non-human form of sociality, subject, and moral agent and its role in emerging psychotic reality.
