papers.authors: Yueqin Wu, Zhipeng Yu

summary.goal: The study examines how international digital discourse constructs the evolving image of Chinese electric vehicles.
summary.methodology: It analyzes large-scale YouTube textual and behavioral data using BERTopic modeling, LLM semantic mapping, the Entropy Weight Method, and social network analysis.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that perceptions have expanded beyond low-cost manufacturing, with intelligent ecosystems strongly activated while cost-effectiveness remains marginal and technological and geopolitical frames form a dual-core configuration.

papers.title: Evaluation of Inductive Coding with LLMs
papers.authors: Leoni Dörfel, Rieke Ammoneit

summary.goal: The study investigates how ChatGPT develops coding systems from interview data through iterative code engineering.
summary.methodology: It compares ChatGPT-generated codes with an inductive content-analysis framework using SBERT similarity, Jaccard overlap, network analysis, and qualitative assessment.
summary.finding: ChatGPT codes often had high cosine similarity but limited overall overlap with human-derived codes, while iterative prompting produced stable systems that remained insufficiently domain-specific.

papers.title: Evaluating Healthcare Provider and Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses to Patient Messages from a Health System Using the CREATE TRUST Framework
papers.authors: Matthew R. Allen, Vijay M. Tiyyala, Armaan Johal, Akhila Chekuri, Elizabeth Conner, Nimit Desai, Kaitlyn Dykes, Tanim Jain

summary.goal: The study compares the clinical substance and communication quality of healthcare provider and AI chatbot responses to cancer patients’ messages.
summary.methodology: Oncologists blindly evaluated triplicate, anonymized responses from healthcare providers, GPT-4, and Mixtral to 189 real-world patient messages using the CREATE TRUST framework.
summary.finding: Overall quality was comparable, with healthcare providers scoring higher on authenticity and tailoring while chatbots scored higher on empathy and referencing.

papers.title: Evaluating AI-generated curriculum designs in vocational education: Evidence from a No-AI diagnostic assessment
papers.authors: Zheng Liu

summary.goal: The study examines how vocational students evaluate AI-generated curriculum designs after using generative AI for course-planning tasks.
summary.methodology: It uses an interpretive single-case study of 39 students whose no-AI handwritten diagnostic assessments were analyzed through thematic, directed content analysis, and holistic judgement levels.
summary.finding: Students recognized broad evaluation criteria and visible implementation problems but less often identified deeper curriculum, assessment, verification, and responsibility issues, revealing a stated-applied judgement gap.

papers.title: Evaluación de metáforas visuales sobre convivencia escolar con inteligencia artificial generativa y juicio experto
papers.authors: Karla Karina Ruiz Mendoza, Luis Horacio Pedroza Zúñiga, Héctor Manuel Rodríguez Figueroa
papers.journal: RELATEC Revista Latinoamericana de Tecnología Educativa

summary.goal: The study compares generative AI models and human experts in evaluating visual metaphors of school coexistence.
summary.methodology: Six human experts and five LLMs rated three metaphors and student explanations using rubric-based measures of agreement, reliability, and generalizability.
summary.finding: Human experts had higher Coexistence Index scores, ChatGPT-5 Pro was closest to human consensus, and one to two human experts plus about ten AI runs achieved generalizability of at least 0.95.

papers.title: Enlighty Politus: a political public opinion dataset from social media in Turkey processed with privacy-preserving AI
papers.authors: Erdem Yörük, Ali Hürriyetoğlu, MEHMET FUAT KINA, Fırat Duruşan, Melih Can Yardı, Şükrü Atsızelti, Tolga Etgü, Emirhan Delen

summary.goal: The paper aims to create a privacy-preserving Turkish political public opinion dataset using social media data and artificial intelligence.
summary.methodology: It integrates deep learning, natural language processing, large language models, computational social science methods, multilevel regression with poststratification, and differential privacy to estimate political indicators across time and location.
summary.finding: The dataset provides granular estimates of ideologies, demographic attributes, and political leader approval while addressing measurement, representation, and privacy concerns.

papers.title: Enhancing EFL learners’ speaking performance through ChatGPT-assisted practice: evidence from complexity, accuracy, and fluency measures
papers.authors: Niloofar Karami, Bahareh Feizarbabi, Ismail Xodabande
papers.journal: Asian-Pacific Journal of Second and Foreign Language Education

summary.goal: The study examined whether ChatGPT-assisted speaking practice improves English as a Foreign Language learners’ speaking development.
summary.methodology: Sixty-five intermediate Iranian learners completed a ten-week quasi-experimental intervention comparing structured ChatGPT-supported practice with teacher-led instruction, using IELTS-aligned speaking tasks and complexity, accuracy, and fluency measures.
summary.finding: ChatGPT-assisted practice improved syntactic complexity and fluency, while accuracy improved in both groups without a distinct between-group advantage.

papers.title: Enacted AI Literacy Towards Epistemic Visibility; Embedding Human-AI Design as Assessment-as-Learning in Pre-Service Science Teachers’ Lesson Redesign
papers.authors: Kallia Katsampoxaki-Hodgetts

summary.goal: The study examines how generative AI mediates science lesson design and reshapes self-regulation, pedagogical agency, and assessment-as-learning among pre-service science teachers.
summary.methodology: It analyzes prompt-based interactions during AI-supported lesson redesign alongside reflective texts using Learning by Design and design-based research frameworks.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that iterative engagement with AI activated planning, monitoring, evaluation, and reflective judgement while making teachers’ reasoning and responsibility visible.

papers.title: Embodied brand companions: fostering passenger loyalty and emotional connection in high-speed rail membership programs via social VR avatars
papers.authors: Xia Hua, Zhou Qin, Congcong Kong, Junping Ding, Zhouyang Gu

summary.goal: The study examines whether an embodied brand avatar in a virtual reality loyalty lounge strengthens passenger loyalty and emotional connection.
summary.methodology: A between-subjects experiment randomly assigned frequent Beijing–Shanghai high-speed rail travelers to embodied-avatar, voice-only, or text-only conditions and measured psychological, behavioral, and physiological outcomes.
summary.finding: The embodied avatar increased social presence, perceived warmth, brand attachment, loyalty intention, and RMSSD relative to the other conditions, with social presence mediating its effect on loyalty intention.

papers.title: Editorial: Revolutionizing nutritional epidemiology: harnessing digital health, AI, and big data for population-level disease prevention and management
papers.authors: Leandro Oliveira, Marta Esgalhado

summary.goal: The editorial examines how digital health, AI, large language models, and big data can advance nutritional epidemiology and population-level disease prevention.
summary.methodology: It synthesizes eleven articles using machine learning, natural language processing, large language models, digital health tools, and other data-driven approaches in nutrition and public health research.
summary.finding: The collection suggests that these technologies enable disease prediction, nutritional surveillance, behavioral analysis, and personalized guidance, while raising concerns about accuracy, bias, privacy, interpretability, and equity.

papers.title: Echoes of Humanity: The Collective Mind of LLM Agents
papers.authors: Daniel dos Santos Salles, Alexandre Reis Graeml
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study investigates whether aggregating judgments from LLM agents can improve email fraud detection through a wisdom-of-crowds approach.
summary.methodology: The researchers collected fraud-likelihood assessments from 122 human agents and 505 LLM agents with varied temperature settings and compared aggregated with individual predictions.
summary.finding: Aggregated LLM-agent judgments generally outperformed individual agents and mitigated errors, although many agents showed a paranoid bias.

papers.title: EXPLAINING TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY STUDENTS' ADOPTION OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN HIGHER EDUCATION: AN INTEGRATED TAM–UTAUT FRAMEWORK USING PLS-SEM AND NECESSARY CONDITION ANALYSIS
papers.authors: Priya SINGH, Mandeep BHARTI, Sushma Rewal CHUGH, Rohit CHAUHAN, Saud Gulzar AHMAD

summary.goal: The study examines factors influencing tourism and hospitality students’ intention to adopt LLM-based learning tools in higher education.
summary.methodology: It surveyed 365 university students in India and analyzed the data using PLS-SEM and Necessary Condition Analysis.
summary.finding: Perceived usefulness, learner motivation, and social influence were identified as important and necessary conditions for high adoption intention.

papers.title: ECHO: An AI-Driven Social Learning Framework for Social Presence in Asynchronous Online Discussions
papers.authors: Xiaojiao Duan
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The paper presents ECHO, a generative-AI framework designed to strengthen social presence and peer engagement in asynchronous online discussions without replacing human interaction.
summary.methodology: It proposes a three-layer Observe–Curate–Humanize workflow and a future three-arm field experiment with approximately 48–60 graduate students, validated surveys, and interviews.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Dual pathways of generative AI use: role ambiguity and self-efficacy in employee-AI collaboration
papers.authors: Qiannan Zhang, Jingyi Zhang, Dong Shan

summary.goal: The study investigates how generative AI use affects employee–AI collaboration through role ambiguity and role breadth self-efficacy, with AI literacy as a moderator.
summary.methodology: The authors surveyed 541 employees in Chinese high-technology firms and tested a structural equation model.
summary.finding: Generative AI use increased both role ambiguity and role breadth self-efficacy, which negatively and positively predicted employee–AI collaboration respectively, while AI literacy moderated both pathways and collaboration was positively associated with job performance.

papers.title: Dual mediating effects of learning motivation and hope on the relationship between generative AI acceptance and learning engagement among Chinese college students: moderated mediation effect of self-directed learning
papers.authors: Yinshun Zhang, Chang Seek Lee, Chao Deng, Xin Liao

summary.goal: The study aimed to examine how generative AI acceptance relates to university students’ learning engagement through learning motivation and hope, with self-directed learning as a moderator.
summary.methodology: The researchers surveyed 478 Chinese university students online and analyzed the data using correlation, structural equation, and moderated mediation analyses.
summary.finding: Generative AI acceptance was positively associated with learning engagement through sequential mediation by learning motivation and hope, while self-directed learning moderated the motivation-to-hope pathway.

papers.title: Does generative AI mean the “end of history” for pharmacovigilance automation? towards a framework for the future of human-AI systems
papers.authors: Leihong Wu, Joshua Xu, Oanh Dang, Robert Ball
papers.journal: Frontiers in Drug Safety and Regulation

summary.goal: The paper develops a framework for understanding how generative AI and LLMs may transform automation in pharmacovigilance while preserving human oversight.
summary.methodology: It presents a conceptual perspective that evaluates pharmacovigilance tasks according to their computational tractability and suitability for automation.
summary.finding: Routine tasks may be automated, but complex causality assessments still require expert judgment, making hybrid human-AI systems preferable to full automation.

papers.title: Do language families matter? Evaluating LLMs for sentiment analysis through a hierarchical cross-lingual lens
papers.authors: Muhamet Kastrati, Abdul Manaf, Ali Shariq Imran, Zenun Kastrati, Sher Muhammad Daudpota, Marenglen Biba

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether language families and resource levels affect LLM performance in multilingual social media sentiment analysis.
summary.methodology: It tests five LLMs on three-class sentiment classification across 36 datasets and languages using zero-shot and few-shot prompting, with hierarchical analysis by language family.
summary.finding: Few-shot prompting generally improves performance, but low-resource languages remain substantially worse served, while GPT-4o and Claude perform best in high- and medium-resource settings.

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Reproduce Question-Wording Effects? A Type-Level Map from Published Split-Ballot Experiments
papers.authors: Howard Kim

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether LLMs can reproduce human responses to different survey question wordings.
summary.methodology: It compares LLM responses from demographic-conditioned panels with response distributions from 56 published split-ballot experiment pairs in the TESS archive.
summary.finding: LLMs directionally reproduced many semantic wording effects but failed to reproduce cognitive-burden effects and should not be used as general-purpose effect estimators.

papers.title: Dissociating communicative success from representational alignment in common ground formation
papers.authors: Taiki Yamamoto, Junya Morita, Ryuichiro Higashinaka, Yugo Takeuchi

summary.goal: The study examines whether successful communication guarantees shared internal representations in human–LLM interaction.
summary.methodology: It compares controlled agent–agent conditions that update perceptual or language-generation modules, with or without discriminative learning, using referent-identification accuracy and feature-space similarity as metrics.
summary.finding: Updating language generation with discrimination improved symbolic alignment but reduced representational alignment, whereas updating perception tended to preserve representational alignment.

papers.title: Development and Query Analysis of an LLM-Powered Police Chatbot with Expert Accuracy Evaluation
papers.authors: Nabila Putri Shalehah, Mohammad Givi Efgivia
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MATHEMATICS AND COMPUTER RESEARCH

summary.goal: The study aims to develop an SOP-compliant police public-service chatbot and analyze user inquiries to identify public needs and trends.
summary.methodology: The system integrates Google Gemini, information retrieval using TF-IDF and cosine similarity, an official SOP database, conversation-log analysis, and evaluations involving black-box tests, IR metrics, experts, and 100 citizens.
summary.finding: The chatbot achieved 95.42% accuracy and high satisfaction ratings from experts (4.83/5) and citizens (4.73/5), outperforming the comparison systems.

papers.title: Development and Preliminary Validation of a Self-Report Scale on Generative AI Literacy in Learning Among High School Students
papers.authors: Diệp Minh Triết Đoàn, Quản Minh Hòa, Chuong Nguyen
papers.journal: Technical Education Science/Giáo dục Kỹ thuật

summary.goal: The study aims to develop and preliminarily validate a self-report scale measuring high school students’ generative AI literacy in learning.
summary.methodology: Survey data from 1,003 students at eight high schools in Ho Chi Minh City were analyzed using Cronbach’s alpha and exploratory factor analysis.
summary.finding: The 23-item scale showed a five-dimensional structure and acceptable internal consistency, with Cronbach’s alpha coefficients ranging from 0.691 to 0.851.

papers.title: Developing and validating the Spanish version of the large language models dependency scale (LLM-D12-SP)
papers.authors: Tran Gia Bao, Mo El-Haj, Sameha Al-Shakhsi, Antonio Garcia-Cabot, Raian Ali, Ala Yankouskaya

summary.goal: The study aims to validate a Spanish instrument measuring psychological dependency on large language models.
summary.methodology: A total of 386 Spanish-speaking participants completed the LLM-D12-SP, which was evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis, reliability, discriminant validity, and external validation analyses.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that the scale supported a two-factor structure with good internal consistency, and that both dependency dimensions were positively associated with internet addiction and perceived LLM trustworthiness.

papers.title: Developing EFL Learners’ Feedback Literacy through AI-Assisted Dialogic Interactions in English Academic Writing: A Mixed-Methods Study
papers.authors: Hong Lei

summary.goal: The study examines how sustained interaction with a GPT-4-based feedback bot develops Chinese EFL university students’ feedback literacy and academic writing.
summary.methodology: It uses a three-week mixed-methods experiment with 45 students, analyzing learner-bot conversations alongside pre-post-delayed tests, essay writing and revision tasks, and interviews.
summary.finding: AI supported 14 feedback-literacy sub-strategies, with Appreciating and Acting-on strategies most frequent and associated with feedback-literacy knowledge and writing quality, while Generating strategies were least used because of cognitive complexity and AI limitations.

papers.title: Detecting and managing participants’ large language model use for open–ended questions in online research
papers.authors: Justus Mann, Jutta Stumpf-Wollersheim

summary.goal: The study examines how participants’ large language model use affects the validity and authenticity of open-ended online research data.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted creative brainstorming studies with 450 Prolific and 442 MTurk participants, using self-reports and activity-monitoring indicators including keystrokes, word-generation rates, webpage exits, and response characteristics.
summary.finding: Indicators of LLM use were associated with more ideas, longer responses, and lower construct reliability, with stronger effects on MTurk than Prolific data.

papers.title: Designing an AI-Enabled Virtual Reality Artifact for Cybersecurity Soft Skill Development: A Design Science Approach
papers.authors: Nicholas Mensah Amoah, Motahareh Pourbehzadi, Moez Farokhnia Hamedani, Lakshmi Iyer
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study aims to develop an AI-enabled virtual reality artifact for cybersecurity soft-skills training.
summary.methodology: It uses a design science approach to create immersive NIST CSF-aligned audit scenarios with generative AI conversational agents that provide mentoring feedback.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings because the artifact is currently being piloted.

papers.title: Designing GenAI-Mediated Mathematics Storybooks: Process Patterns and Tool Affordance Uptake Among Pre-Service Early Childhood Teachers
papers.authors: Yau Yu Chan, Kwok Man Keith Ho

summary.goal: The study examines how pre-service early childhood educators use GenAI to design mathematics storybooks while maintaining pedagogical control.
summary.methodology: It uses exploratory qualitative cross-case workflow analysis of 27 Hong Kong pre-service educators’ presentations, ChatGPT and Krea interaction records, and completed storybooks.
summary.finding: Participants used pedagogical constraints, explored alternatives, and critically selected and revised outputs, following two recurring workflows while balancing efficiency, creativity, coherence, and local contextual fit.

papers.title: Designing AI Sandboxes for Human-Machine Pedagogies
papers.authors: Jacob Holster

summary.goal: The chapter examines how generative AI can be integrated into music teacher education to support creative, pedagogical, ethical, and professional development.
summary.methodology: It uses design-based research and two case studies involving a creative-production AI sandbox and a GPT-powered classroom-rehearsal simulation with preservice and undergraduate music students.
summary.finding: The studies suggest that AI sandboxes can support multimodal fluency, reflective inquiry, creative engagement, relational ethics, and pedagogical decision-making.

papers.title: Design Principles for a Risk-Aware Conversational Agent in Digital Mental Health Information Access: The Case of Cognitive Theatre
papers.authors: Yiming Zhou, Mahsa Honary, Amjad Fayoumi

summary.goal: The study aims to develop a risk-aware conversational agent for digital mental health information access and interaction.
summary.methodology: Using Design Science Research Methodology, the authors developed and evaluated Cognitive Theatre, a controller-mediated, role-decomposed agent informed by cognitive behavioural therapy.
summary.finding: Under controlled model-generated conditions, the system escalated all 50 extreme-risk inputs and received higher ratings than two baselines in AI-based and limited human evaluations.

papers.title: DEFINED: A Data-Efficient Computational Framework for Fine-Grained Creativity Assessment in Debate Scenarios
papers.authors: Tongzhou Yu, Mingjia Li, Hong Qian, Wenkai Wang, Zongbao Zhang, Yaoyu Jiang, Xiangfeng Wang, Aimin Zhou

summary.goal: The paper aims to develop a data-efficient framework for fine-grained creativity assessment in debate scenarios.
summary.methodology: It uses a pretrained autoregressive language model with a hierarchical scoring head, authentic debate data and expert annotations, constrained data augmentation, mixed-granularity training, and a study with debate-naive participants.
summary.finding: The scoring model achieves accurate and stable scoring and outperforms prompt-based large language model evaluators and existing debate-scoring methods.

papers.title: CropChain: An AI-Powered Agricultural Social Platform Integrating Rice Disease Detection, Expert Collaboration, and Digital Marketplace Services for Smallholder Farmers
papers.authors: Author unavailable
papers.journal: Trends in Animal and Plant Sciences

summary.goal: The study aims to develop an integrated agricultural platform combining rice-disease detection, an Urdu LLM advisory chatbot, expert collaboration, and a marketplace for Pakistani smallholder farmers.
summary.methodology: The authors trained and compared three image-classification models and assessed user acceptance through a 54-item questionnaire completed by 52 respondents from Pakistan’s rice-growing region.
summary.finding: Respondents rated the platform positively, with 94.2% agreeing that combining AI, expert, and community input supports better decisions than AI alone.

papers.title: Credibility attacks do not enhance the impact of deepfake warnings
papers.authors: Emily R. Spearing, Kaitlin Norgard, Simon Clark, Stephan Lewandowsky, Ullrich K. H. Ecker

summary.goal: The study examines whether undermining a witness’s credibility enhances the effectiveness of warnings about deepfake videos.
summary.methodology: Across two experiments with 2,500 participants, researchers measured guilt judgments after exposure to a deepfake criminal accusation with warnings and witness credibility manipulations involving accents and character descriptions.
summary.finding: Deepfake exposure increased guilt judgments, warnings only partially reduced this effect, and adding witness discreditation did not improve warning effectiveness.

papers.title: Crafting Effective Prompts: Thinking with Machines Not Just Talking to Them
papers.authors: Ekta Sinha, Shalini Chandra, Charles Waghmare

summary.goal: The chapter aims to provide a conceptual and practical approach to crafting effective prompts for using generative AI and LLMs in academia.
summary.methodology: It categorizes informational, instructional, creative, and conversational prompts and discusses iterative prompting using insights from emerging prompt-engineering and human–AI interaction research.
summary.finding: The chapter argues that specificity, context, structure, and iterative refinement can improve outputs and support scholarly thinking, while noting risks of superficial coherence and epistemic unreliability.

papers.title: Coordinating Meaning with AI System Cards: A Thematic Analysis
papers.authors: Jennifer Rene French Cyrek

summary.goal: The study examines how AI developers use system cards to frame risk and responsible development in public discourse.
summary.methodology: It conducts a thematic content analysis of a purposive corpus of AI system cards from 2023–2025 using coordinated management of meaning theory.
summary.finding: The analysis finds that system cards prioritize catastrophic risks, omit broader societal harms such as declining critical thinking, and use scientific conventions and benchmarks to build trust through transparency.

papers.title: Contextualizing Teacher AI Literacy in English Language Teaching: Developing an AI Literacy Framework for College English Teachers
papers.authors: Wang Miao, Yun TianYing

summary.goal: The study aims to develop a contextualized AI literacy framework for college English teachers.
summary.methodology: Researchers combined existing competency frameworks with semi-structured interviews with eight university English teachers and thematic analysis.
summary.finding: The study identifies five dimensions and fifteen domains of teacher AI literacy shaped by English teaching objectives, language learning principles, and professional knowledge.

papers.title: Contextualized sensorimotor norms: Multi-dimensional measures of sensorimotor strength for ambiguous English words, in context
papers.authors: Sean Trott, Benjamin K. Bergen

summary.goal: The study introduces contextualized sensorimotor norms for ambiguous English words and evaluates whether GPT-4 can recover sensorimotor information.
summary.methodology: Researchers collected human ratings for 112 words in four contexts and compared them with existing norms, semantic-relatedness judgments, and GPT-4 ratings.
summary.finding: Contextualized ratings captured distinct information, reflected word meanings and semantic relatedness, and GPT-4 ratings aligned reasonably well with human judgments.

papers.title: Constructing a Blended Foreign Language Teaching Model Empowered by Generative Artificial Intelligence and Integrating Local Chinese Culture
papers.authors: Hua Li
papers.journal: English Language Teaching and Linguistics Studies

summary.goal: The study aims to construct a blended foreign-language teaching model that uses generative AI to integrate local Chinese culture and improve students’ linguistic, cultural, and intercultural competencies.
summary.methodology: It uses an English Pronunciation course and Shaoxing culture as a case example, guided by the Production-Oriented Approach.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Comparison of artificial intelligence assisted training and traditional learning paths in clinical simulation skills training: meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
papers.authors: Sihan Che, Huan Zhao, Tianlin Lu, Zhen You

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether AI-assisted clinical simulation training improves skills, procedure time, and learner satisfaction compared with traditional instruction.
summary.methodology: The authors conducted a meta-analysis of 12 randomized controlled trials comparing AI-assisted and traditional clinical skills training.
summary.finding: AI-assisted training improved overall clinical skills and learner satisfaction, but large language models showed no statistically significant advantage over traditional training.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Emotion Prediction in Reviews of Large Language Model-Powered Applications
papers.authors: Semmy Wellem Taju, George Morris William Tangka, Ibrena Reghuella Chrisanti
papers.journal: Advances in Human Resource Management Research

summary.goal: The study aims to compare conventional machine-learning algorithms for classifying emotions in user reviews of LLM-powered applications.
summary.methodology: Researchers scraped Google Play Store reviews of eight LLM applications, labeled them into five emotion categories, and evaluated ten algorithms using TF-IDF features and multiple performance metrics.
summary.finding: XGBoost performed best, achieving 87.30% accuracy and demonstrating strong discrimination across emotion classes.

papers.title: Combining implementation and data sciences to accelerate evidence integration into healthcare – ImpleMATE
papers.authors: J. Chan, Janna Hastings, Gabriella Tiernan, Jeannie Paterson, Nigel H. Lovell, Luc Betbeder-Matibet, Patrick Kin Man Tung, Sarah Pink

summary.goal: The study aims to develop an AI-assisted platform to accelerate the integration of research evidence into routine healthcare practice.
summary.methodology: The platform will be co-designed using human-centred methods and will combine an implementation-focused ontology, AI knowledge extraction, an interactive decision-support application, and an evaluation framework.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Cognitive Entanglement: Toward a Developmental Framework of the Human-AI Coevolutionary Leap
papers.authors: Xiao-Kun Wu, Min Chen, Giancarlo Fortino

summary.goal: The article proposes a developmental framework for understanding how sustained human–AI interaction changes users’ cognitive capacities.
summary.methodology: It develops the concept of cognitive entanglement by drawing on philosophy of mind, cognitive science, and learning science to compare forms of human–AI coupling.
summary.finding: The article argues that repeated AI delegation may weaken independent judgment or reorganize cognition, while AI designed to provide productive challenge could support cognitive development.

papers.title: Climate-control ChatGPT for EFL writing and AI literacy
papers.authors: Hesham Aldamen, Salwa Mohammad Alawneh, Mohamad Almashour, Mutasim Al-Deaibes, Rami Alsharefeen

summary.goal: The study examines whether a prompting design requiring learners to justify, qualify, counterexample, and re-author claims improves AI literacy, harm-sensitive reasoning, and independent argumentative writing among EFL students.
summary.methodology: A mixed-methods quasi-experiment assigned 120 Jordanian undergraduates to no-ChatGPT, standard ChatGPT, or climate-control ChatGPT conditions and analyzed essays, dialogue logs, drafts, reflections, interviews, and annotated language units.
summary.finding: The climate-control condition produced the largest gains in harm-sensitive AI literacy and argumentative writing, maintained delayed no-AI transfer, reduced direct uptake, increased self-repair and authorial control, and improved distinctions between AI competence and consciousness.

papers.title: Clause Encounters of the Third Kind: Can LLMs Replace Language Teachers?
papers.authors: Kristina Šekrst, Ana Kovačić

summary.goal: The paper evaluates whether large language models can provide the corrective feedback and methodological explanations needed for language learning.
summary.methodology: It tests multiple models on identifying, correcting, and explaining English learner mistakes while varying model parameters and using retrieval-augmented generation, evaluated with automated metrics and expert judgments.
summary.finding: Models show strong surface-level correction abilities, but their explanations often lack the terminology and domain knowledge required for effective teaching.

papers.title: Chatbots reduce health-related conspiracy beliefs not because of but despite being perceived as AI
papers.authors: Paul Ballot, Yana van de Sande, Hanna Schraffenberger, Philipp Schmid

summary.goal: The study examines whether LLM-driven debates reduce COVID-19 health conspiracy beliefs and whether source attribution explains their effectiveness.
summary.methodology: In an online experiment, 554 participants debated a COVID-19 conspiracy theory with an AI-labelled LLM, a human-labelled LLM, or no chatbot control.
summary.finding: Both chatbot conditions reduced conspiracy confidence, with larger reductions when participants believed they were interacting with a human, apparently mediated by perceived source neutrality.

papers.title: ChatbotLab: An Open Framework for Human-Like Chatbot Interaction and Survey Data Collection
papers.authors: Salvatore Giorgi, João Sedoc, Abhay P Singh, Oscar Kjell, Soojin Lee, Lyle Ungar

summary.goal: The paper presents ChatbotLab, an open-source framework for deploying LLM-powered chatbot conversations in behavioral research and survey studies.
summary.methodology: It describes an end-to-end software package integrated with crowdsourcing and survey platforms, supporting configurable conversations, secure data linkage, reproducible records, moderation, data export, and load testing.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: ChatGPT-5 as a leisure health advisor: multidimensional assessment of reliability, quality, usefulness and readability
papers.authors: Alican Bayram

summary.goal: The study aims to assess ChatGPT-5’s reliability, quality, usefulness, and readability when providing non-clinical leisure health advice.
summary.methodology: Researchers generated ChatGPT-5 responses to 34 leisure-and-health questions and evaluated them using mDISCERN, GQS, a usefulness Likert scale, and the Flesch Reading Ease formula.
summary.finding: ChatGPT-5 showed moderate reliability, good quality, and relatively high usefulness, but difficult readability, inconsistent source transparency, and limitations with personalized scenarios constrained its utility.

papers.title: ChatGPT for Intelligent Human–AI Interaction: Opportunities and Limitations
papers.authors: Dr. Antoine Morel, Dr. Camille Laurent
papers.journal: International Bulletin of Applied Sciences and Technology

summary.goal: The paper reviews ChatGPT’s opportunities and limitations for intelligent human–AI collaboration.
summary.methodology: It conducts a qualitative review and comparative synthesis of twelve scholarly references.
summary.finding: The review finds that ChatGPT is versatile across domains but faces persistent challenges involving hallucination, explainability, accuracy, and responsible deployment.

papers.title: ChatGPT and Large Language Models in Contemporary Nursing
papers.authors: Izabella Uchmanowicz, Heba Aldossary, Christopher S. Lee, Mariachiara Figura, Maria Jędrzejczyk, Maddalena De Maria, Gianluca Pucciarelli, Ewa Molka

summary.goal: The review synthesizes evidence on ChatGPT and LLM applications, benefits, limitations, and governance in nursing education, clinical practice, and workflow management.
summary.methodology: The authors conducted a narrative review of literature identified through structured searches of Medline, Scopus, and arXiv from January 2019 to March 2026.
summary.finding: LLMs may support nursing education, preliminary clinical assessment, patient education, and documentation, but hallucinations, bias, privacy risks, accountability concerns, and limited performance in complex cases require human verification and governed deployment.

papers.title: Characterizing Agentic Flooding of Government Services
papers.authors: Chris Schmitz, Lewis Hammond, Alan Chan

summary.goal: The paper examines how AI agents and large language models may create surges in demand for government services and strain service capacity.
summary.methodology: The authors analyze 84 potential flooding cases across 11 jurisdictions and develop a risk matrix and response framework.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that flooding likely occurs widely, poses greatest near-term risk to financially attractive and complex services, and may prompt access-reducing responses such as fees.

papers.title: Characterization and Effects of CS2 Learning with GenAI, Visualization, and Human Support
papers.authors: Quinton Yong, Miguel A. Nacenta, Anthony Estey

summary.goal: The study examines how generative AI compares with algorithm visualization and human tutoring as learning supports in an advanced computer science course.
summary.methodology: Twelve students completed three 90-minute sessions on algorithms using each support, while researchers recorded gaze and interaction data and assessed conceptual understanding afterward.
summary.finding: Generative AI increased self-efficacy more than live tutoring but produced lower learning outcomes, while live tutoring yielded the strongest learning results.

papers.title: Can’t help falling in love… with a bot? A mixed-methods analysis of public discourses of AI intimacy and companionship on YouTube
papers.authors: Anurag Shekhar, Calvin Mabaso

summary.goal: The study examines how AI intimacy and companionship are publicly debated in YouTube comments.
summary.methodology: It analyzes 8,757 comments using sentiment, emotion, and topic modeling, alongside reflexive thematic analysis of 527 high-engagement comments.
summary.finding: The comments portray AI companionship as both emotionally supportive and potentially limiting, while raising concerns about authenticity, loneliness, social conditions, and commercial exploitation of intimate disclosures.

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Support University Counseling? Evidence from Perceived Counseling Alliance, Disclosure Willingness, and Risk Recognition
papers.authors: Jianshan Cheng

summary.goal: The study examined whether an LLM-based counseling agent improves perceived counseling alliance, disclosure willingness, and recognition of mental health risks among Chinese university students.
summary.methodology: Using a randomized between-subjects experiment, the researchers compared 388 students assigned to an LLM-based counseling condition or a control condition.
summary.finding: The LLM agent improved counseling alliance, disclosure willingness, and general risk recognition, but showed limited performance for crisis-level disclosures and was best suited as complementary front-end support.

papers.title: Bridging Coursework and Professional Practice through a Retrieval-Grounded, Privacy-Preserving AI Learning Companion
papers.authors: Chen Ying
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Canadian Engineering Education Association (CEEA)

summary.goal: The paper aims to design a privacy-preserving AI learning companion that supports guided exploration of professional codebases in large graduate engineering courses.
summary.methodology: It presents a retrieval-grounded system using hybrid lexical-semantic retrieval, chunk-level indexing, and a locally hosted 8B-parameter language model, along with a planned classroom evaluation.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Bias or Memory? Contamination-Controlled Measurement of Behavioral Biases in Large Language Models
papers.authors: Stavros Vlachos

summary.goal: The project aims to measure behavioral biases in large language models while distinguishing learned biases from memorization or contamination effects.
summary.methodology: It compares responses to verbatim canonical vignettes and novel-surface isomorphs across human-lives, non-human, and monetary stakes, using a preregistered analysis of 5,800 pilot trials.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Beyond Empathy: Emotional Intelligence and Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Social Work Practice, Therapeutic Alliance and Human Services
papers.authors: Gary Bailey

summary.goal: The review examines the relationship between emotional intelligence and artificial intelligence and implications for clinical social work, therapeutic alliance, ethical decision-making, and service delivery.
summary.methodology: It conducts an integrative review of peer-reviewed literature from 2020 to 2026 across social work, psychology, psychiatry, counseling, affective computing, human-computer interaction, and artificial intelligence.
summary.finding: The review finds that AI can recognize and simulate emotions and support emotional-intelligence development, but simulated empathy differs from authentic therapeutic relationships and raises ethical concerns.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: A Mixed-Methods Audit of Chain-of-Thought Failures in LLM-Based COVID-19 Vaccine Stance Detection
papers.authors: Andreas Praschk, Valentin Fischill-Neudeck, Thomas Caspari, Hans‐Peter Wiesinger

summary.goal: The study assessed whether reasoning-enabled LLMs can classify COVID-19 vaccination stances and produce coherent, auditable reasoning for public health research.
summary.methodology: The authors evaluated zero-shot stance classification by o4-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash on 3,060 human-annotated vaccination tweets and qualitatively analyzed shared misclassifications and chain-of-thought summaries.
summary.finding: Both models achieved macro-F1 scores around 0.8, but shared errors included target confusion, literal interpretations of sarcasm, and mismatches between labels and rationales.

papers.title: Awareness of academic paper retractions and artificial intelligence–related risks among health researchers in Jordan: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Rana Abu Farha, Lobna Gharaibeh, Karem H. Alzoubi, Muna Barakat, Khawla Abu Hammour, Fahmi Y. Al-Ashwal

summary.goal: The study examined health researchers’ awareness of academic retractions and risks associated with using AI tools.
summary.methodology: It used a validated online cross-sectional questionnaire completed by 255 health researchers in Jordan.
summary.finding: Although 73.3% reported using AI tools, major concerns included fabricated references and data, while many researchers rarely checked whether cited articles had been retracted.

papers.title: Attitudes on AI Adoptions: Input to Policy Formulation
papers.authors: Ramil Santos
papers.journal: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

summary.goal: The study evaluates how AI is used for oral and written higher-education tasks and informs policy formulation in the Philippines.
summary.methodology: It uses qualitative grounded theory and the Delphi method with students, teachers, and administrators from four higher-education institutions in Bulacan.
summary.finding: AI was used for brainstorming, editing, lesson development, material preparation, and documentation, but participants reported plagiarism, excessive reliance, and reduced original thought, supporting the need for national policies and greater awareness.

papers.title: Associations between generative AI–based pronunciation feedback and willingness to communicate in English: the mediating role of English pronunciation self-efficacy
papers.authors: Yang Lu, Yanchao Yang, Tianxue Cui, Zeyang Yang, Yuanyuan Cai, Bosheng Jing

summary.goal: The study examines how perceptions of generative AI-based pronunciation feedback relate to English willingness to communicate and whether pronunciation self-efficacy mediates this relationship.
summary.methodology: A cross-sectional survey of 1,701 Chinese university English learners was analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling and bias-corrected bootstrapping.
summary.finding: Positive perceptions of generative AI feedback were associated with greater willingness to communicate, with pronunciation self-efficacy partially mediating the relationship and accounting for 69.9% of the total effect.

papers.title: Assessing faculty knowledge, attitudes, practices, and training needs regarding artificial intelligence in medical education
papers.authors: Nouran Nader Elnemr, Soha Rashed Aref, Aly Mohamed Abdelmohsen, Nadia Abdelmoneim Elzeiny, Ayat Eltayar

summary.goal: The study aimed to assess medical educators’ knowledge, attitudes, practices, and training needs regarding AI to inform faculty development planning.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted a web-based cross-sectional survey of 336 faculty members and teaching assistants, analyzing quantitative responses descriptively and qualitative responses through content analysis.
summary.finding: Although many respondents were interested in AI, most lacked awareness and experience, citing limited access, insufficient knowledge, and inadequate training opportunities as key barriers, with workshops preferred for training.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based positive youth development intervention protocol in school settings
papers.authors: Mehmet Akif Karaman, Ashraf Mahmud

summary.goal: The paper aims to outline an eight-week AI-supported positive youth development intervention for high school students and a feasibility-oriented mixed-method evaluation design.
summary.methodology: The intervention combines daily AI micro-nudges, voluntary micro-coaching dialogues, weekly counselor sessions, pre–post trait measures, daily ecological momentary assessments, quantitative effect-size and Tau-U analyses, and qualitative thematic analysis.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence dependency in college students: a critical narrative review
papers.authors: Xuehua He, Shan Li, Ren Cha, Li Wang, Yunxia Shen, Ruijuan Wu, Lili Wu, Xiaoyan Gong

summary.goal: The review examines AI dependency among college students, including its conceptualization, determinants, consequences, measurement, and interventions.
summary.methodology: It conducts a critical narrative review of evidence from the past decade on students’ use of generative AI and LLM applications.
summary.finding: The literature suggests that cognitive delegation, emotional reliance, and reduced self-regulation may accompany AI dependency, while assessment remains fragmented and interventions should emphasize augmentation, AI literacy, and critical evaluation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence companionship for loneliness in older adults: An interview with Vijeth Iyengar and Elizabeth Broadbent
papers.authors: Priyam Joshi, Anna Rader, Shreya Venkatesh

summary.goal: The paper examines whether AI companions could address loneliness and support health among older adults.
summary.methodology: It presents an interview with experts in human-robot interaction, aging, and brain health.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and teacher competence: a scoping review of assessment, analytics, and professional development
papers.authors: Nurseit Baizhanov, Batyr Sharimbayev, Zhairan Churbanova, Akzhan Khaidarova, Lyazzat Shinetova

summary.goal: The review maps how artificial intelligence is connected to teacher competence in assessment, analytics, and professional development.
summary.methodology: It conducts a scoping review of 33 peer-reviewed articles published from 2022 to 2026 and identified through a bounded Web of Science search.
summary.finding: The literature emphasizes AI-based competence assessment and teacher AI literacy but reports limited explainable AI, fairness analysis, multimodal validation, and longitudinal research.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Journalism and Media Practice: A Systematic Review of Applications, Limitations, and Research Approaches
papers.authors: Jun Gui, Nasrullah Dharejo, Mumtaz Aini Alivi

summary.goal: The study investigates applications, limitations, and research approaches concerning AI and machine learning in journalism and media practice.
summary.methodology: It systematically reviewed 121 peer-reviewed articles using PRISMA, qualitative thematic analysis, structural topic modelling, and bibliometric network analysis.
summary.finding: The review finds that effective AI adoption depends on workflow redesign and human–machine collaboration, while audience responses to AI-generated content vary across cultures and copyright frameworks remain contested.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Human Development: Integrating Humanities, Education, and Intelligent Information Systems
papers.authors: Norman Ralph B. Isla
papers.journal: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science

summary.goal: The article examines how humanities, education, and intelligent information systems can support human-centered AI for sustainable human development.
summary.methodology: It reviews and synthesizes recent research on cultural values, fairness, trust, AI literacy, generative AI, assessment, sustainability, interpretability, climate action, and healthcare.
summary.finding: It argues that AI should complement human capacities through inclusive, accountable, transparent, human-monitored, and culturally responsive socio-technical systems.

papers.title: ArchiveGPT: A human-centered evaluation of using a vision language model for image cataloguing
papers.authors: Line Abele, Gerrit Anders, Tolgahan Aydın, Jürgen Buder, Helen Fischer, Dominik Kimmel, Markus Huff

summary.goal: The study examines whether AI-generated catalogue descriptions approximate human-written quality and how generative AI could support archival and museum cataloguing workflows.
summary.methodology: InternVL2 generated descriptions of archaeological photographs, which experts and non-experts evaluated after human curation by classifying authorship, rating quality, and reporting willingness to use and trust AI tools.
summary.finding: Participants performed above chance at identifying AI descriptions, while OCR errors and hallucinations reduced quality perceptions and experts showed lower willingness to adopt AI, supporting human verification and transparent collaboration.

papers.title: An Integrated Human and Digital Communication Model for AI-Empowered Translation Education
papers.authors: Minna Liang, Anurak Panyanuwat

summary.goal: The study aims to develop an integrated model for translation learning through structured human–AI engagement and teacher guidance.
summary.methodology: It combines communication, educational, digital literacy, and critical-thinking frameworks and evaluates the model through a preliminary assessment by five domain specialists.
summary.finding: Experts provided initial support for the model’s coherence, utility, understandability, and acceptability, while classroom effectiveness remains untested.

papers.title: An External Governance Framework for AI Roles in Large Language Model Interaction
papers.authors: Qian Ma, Kaixuan Liu, Yongdong Zhou
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper proposes an external governance framework to make LLM-based AI roles more deterministic, verifiable, and auditable in human–AI interaction.
summary.methodology: Using a design science approach, it develops the Role Base framework with semantic layers, governance mechanisms, external constraints, and output-based drift measures.
summary.finding: The framework provides a theoretical and technical design for governed AI roles, but its effectiveness awaits prototype implementation and empirical validation.

papers.title: Aligning ChatGPT with e-portfolio assessment as EFL learning model: Its effect on student’s speaking performance and feedback literacy
papers.authors: I Putu Yoga Laksana, Ni Made Ratminingsih, Made Hery Santosa, I Putu Indra Kusuma

summary.goal: The study examines whether integrating ChatGPT with e-portfolio assessment improves students’ speaking performance and feedback literacy in an English course.
summary.methodology: Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, the study compared 60 students receiving ChatGPT-integrated e-portfolio assessment with a control group using conventional e-portfolios, drawing on speaking tests, questionnaires, and interviews.
summary.finding: ChatGPT-integrated e-portfolio assessment significantly improved speaking performance and feedback literacy, with interview analysis identifying seven related themes.

papers.title: Algorithmic amplification of geopolitical narratives and user engagement in the 2024 U. S. presidential election
papers.authors: Ahmed Hassan

summary.goal: The study examines how geopolitical narratives in 2024 U.S. presidential campaign videos were associated with YouTube user engagement.
summary.methodology: Researchers used GPT-4, BERT, RoBERTa, human verification, and statistical models to analyze 5,466 campaign-related YouTube videos.
summary.finding: Geopolitical, threat-framed, national-security, patriotic, and negatively sentimented content was associated with higher engagement, especially immigration and border-security content.

papers.title: Algorithmic Justice and Responsible AI Journalism: A Comparative Communication Policy Perspective in East Asia
papers.authors: Renxiudi Huang, Linjia Bai

summary.goal: The study compares how China and South Korea regulate algorithmic fairness and platform accountability in AI journalism.
summary.methodology: It conducts comparative textual analysis of policy documents and examines evidence from Toutiao and Naver.
summary.finding: Both regulatory models mitigate infodemics and algorithmic bias but involve trade-offs between regulatory efficiency and editorial independence.

papers.title: Agentic AI as a Driver of Innovation and Change Management in Organizations: A Conceptual Review and Framework for Technology-Enabled Transformation
papers.authors: Fatma Albalooshi
papers.journal: International Journal of Technology and Systems

summary.goal: The paper examines how Agentic AI may drive organizational innovation and change management during technology-enabled transformation.
summary.methodology: It uses a desk-based conceptual review and framework development based on a structured literature search and thematic synthesis.
summary.finding: Agentic AI may support ideation, experimentation, process redesign, and workflow coordination, but successful transformation requires organizational readiness, employee trust, human oversight, and responsible governance.

papers.title: Ageism in Human-AI Social Interaction: A Scoping Review of Age Bias in Large Language Model Chatbots for Older Adults
papers.authors: Soni Rudi Hartanto, Suwarni, Ramadhani Ulansari, Yudhi Biantoro, Suharyanto, Taufikur Ramadhan

summary.goal: The study examines ageism in large language model chatbots and proposes a framework for detecting and reducing age bias.
summary.methodology: It conducts a PRISMA-ScR systematic evaluation of 12 papers published between 2023 and 2026 and develops a dual-stage debiasing framework.
summary.finding: The review identifies explicit ageist values and condescending conversational styles in LLMs, while finding that standard benchmarks often miss these interactional biases.

papers.title: After the Interface: Relocating Human Agency in the Age of Conversational AI
papers.authors: Mengke Wu, Mike Yao

summary.goal: The paper aims to reconceptualize human agency in conversational, generative, and agentic AI systems.
summary.methodology: It revisits control as a diagnostic lens, distinguishes process control from outcome control, and maps systems across these dimensions conceptually.
summary.finding: The paper argues that agency is redistributed from interface affordances to interaction through goal articulation, output evaluation, and outcome negotiation.

papers.title: Affordances and Challenges of GenAI Feedback in Primary Students’ Scientific Drawing
papers.authors: Kason Ka Ching Cheung, Chen Jiahao Enzo, Young Hoan Cho, Zhi Hong Wan, Cheung Ho Wai, Pang Wai Fung

summary.goal: The study aims to design effective GenAI feedback to improve primary students’ scientific drawings and practices.
summary.methodology: Researchers developed the Sci-GiFD application and conducted a mixed-method case study with 65 Year 3 students over six days, analyzing pre- and post-drawings, 404 drawing records, feedback, and GenAI scoring accuracy.
summary.finding: Students’ topic-specific scientific model drawings improved, and qualitative evidence showed that some students acted on GenAI feedback to revise their observational and model drawings.

papers.title: Adoption of generative artificial intelligence in instruction: a mixed-methods UTAUT study of K-12 computer science teachers in China
papers.authors: Shu Zhao, Chunchen Kang, Wanshan Hu, Zhijuan Feng

summary.goal: The study examines factors influencing K-12 computer science teachers’ adoption of generative AI in instruction in China.
summary.methodology: It uses a mixed-methods design combining structural equation modeling of survey data from 338 teachers across 20 provinces with thematic analysis of concept map-supported interviews with 12 teachers.
summary.finding: Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, innovation expectation, cost-benefit, attitude, and perceived risk shaped adoption intentions, while interviews identified concerns about teacher authority, student overreliance, limited understanding, and data security.

papers.title: Addressing longstanding challenges in cognitive science with language models
papers.authors: Dirk U. Wulff, Rui Mata

summary.goal: The paper examines how language models could address longstanding challenges in cognitive science research integration, formalization, conceptual clarity, and analysis of naturalistic data.
summary.methodology: It presents a conceptual discussion of potential applications and risks of using language models in cognitive science.
summary.finding: The paper concludes that language models could support a more integrative and cumulative cognitive science when used judiciously alongside human researchers.

papers.title: Addicted to AI? Prevalence and psychological drivers of generative AI dependency among pre-service teachers
papers.authors: Bin Jiang, Zhuo Wang

summary.goal: The study examines the prevalence and psychological drivers of generative AI dependency among pre-service teachers and whether perceived AI literacy is protective.
summary.methodology: It uses a mixed-methods design combining an online survey of 565 education-major students in Chinese teacher-preparation programs with interviews of five participants and structural and necessary-condition analyses.
summary.finding: Dependency was widespread and was driven primarily by impulsivity and anthropomorphic attachment, while perceived AI literacy had a modest protective effect and social norms were a necessary condition.

papers.title: AI-generated videos in medical science popularization and education: a scoping review
papers.authors: Jiejia Ma, Xiujun Zheng, Lijin Wang, Jiachun Wu, Zimo Yang, Siyu Wei, Ruibin Huang

summary.goal: The review aimed to synthesize research on AI-generated videos for public, patient, medical student, and physician education and propose a production framework.
summary.methodology: The authors conducted a scoping review of studies identified through four databases and screened according to Arksey and O’Malley and PRISMA-ScR guidelines.
summary.finding: The reviewed studies were few and heterogeneous, with inconsistent prompts and evaluation methods and generally low video quality scores for patient education.

papers.title: AI-generated food stimuli match real counterparts in perceived healthiness and calorie content but not in realism or willingness to eat
papers.authors: Alexander Diel, Leonardo Pimpini, Giuseppe Marrazzo, Finley Sam Mellis, Niels Weber, Tania Josan Lalgi, Laura Bäuerle, Martin Teufel

summary.goal: The study examines whether AI-generated food images are perceived similarly to real food images in terms of realism, willingness to eat, calorie content, and healthiness.
summary.methodology: In a within-subject online experiment, 87 participants rated 60 matched pairs of AI-generated and pre-validated real food images on four visual analogue scales.
summary.finding: AI-generated images were rated as less realistic and less appealing to eat, while perceived healthiness and calorie content did not differ from real images.

papers.title: AI-Supported Scaffold Design for Lower-Proficiency EFL Learners: Experiences of Pre-Service Teachers in Inclusive Reading Instruction
papers.authors: Dieu Bich Nguyen, An Hoai Thi Le
papers.journal: Vietnam Journal of Education (online)/Vietnam Journal of Education/Giáo dục

summary.goal: The study examines how pre-service teachers use generative AI to design scaffolding materials for lower-proficiency learners in inclusive EFL reading instruction.
summary.methodology: It uses a qualitative design involving seven pre-service teachers and 22 learners over an eight-week practicum, analyzing lesson plans, scaffold artifacts, reflective journals, and interviews thematically.
summary.finding: AI-generated lexical, procedural, conceptual, and affective scaffolds were associated with greater learner participation, confidence, reading-strategy use, and engagement, although teachers needed to adapt the materials to classroom contexts.

papers.title: AI-GENERATED CONTEXTUAL LISTENING MATERIALS EXPLORING TEACHER AND STUDENTS PERCEPTIONS IN EFL CLASSROOMS
papers.authors: Mikael Albinus Silitonga, Dedi Irwan, Rahayu Meliasari

summary.goal: The study explores students’ and a teacher’s perceptions of AI-generated contextual listening materials in an EFL classroom.
summary.methodology: Researchers used a descriptive qualitative design involving interviews and observations of three ninth-grade students and one English teacher, analyzed thematically.
summary.finding: Students reported greater confidence and comprehension from familiar local content, while the teacher valued customization but noted inconsistent audio clarity and the need for human editing and feedback.

papers.title: AI-Based Resume Screening and Job Matching Systems: A Comprehensive Review of NLP, Machine Learning, Explainable AI, and Fairness-Aware Recruitment Approaches
papers.authors: Naveen J, Manoj M, Jayanth Vishwakarma G

summary.goal: The paper reviews how AI, including large language models, supports resume screening and job matching while addressing efficiency, explainability, and fairness.
summary.methodology: It surveys approaches including TF-IDF, cosine similarity, transformers, neural networks, and large language models across hiring environments.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that AI can improve screening efficiency and job matching but raises concerns about bias, opacity, privacy, and the need for human oversight.

papers.title: AI-Based Reflection on Character Strengths at Work: Testing a Digital Strengths Intervention in a Randomized Controlled Study
papers.authors: Lara Watermann, Ricarda Kochems, Eva Lermer, Simone Kubowitsch
papers.journal: International Journal of Applied Positive Psychology

summary.goal: The study tested whether AI-supported reflection on character strengths improves strengths use and adaptive functioning at work.
summary.methodology: In a randomized controlled trial, 111 working adults received AI-supported reflection, unaided self-reflection, or waitlist control across three weekly assessments.
summary.finding: Neither intervention significantly improved primary outcomes, but strengths-related lexical density in the AI condition predicted later strengths use.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Analysis of PowerPoint Slides: A Methodological Approach to Decolonising Business Education
papers.authors: Timothy Groves, Jordan Allison, Omar El Masri

summary.goal: The study develops a reproducible AI-assisted workflow for identifying and auditing colonial markers in MBA lecture slides.
summary.methodology: It used expert review, AI-assisted analysis, thematic synthesis, and exploratory Langflow- and LangChain-Python-based workflows to analyze teaching materials.
summary.finding: AI-generated markers substantially converged with expert-identified markers, although technical limitations constrained effectiveness and outputs were considered useful for reflective curriculum review.

papers.title: AI usage patterns and self-rated critical thinking among Chinese college students: the moderating role of academic motivation
papers.authors: J M Zhang, Yang Yang

summary.goal: The study examines how different AI usage patterns relate to Chinese university students’ perceived critical thinking and how academic motivation moderates these relationships.
summary.methodology: A cross-sectional survey of 342 undergraduate students measured information retrieval, content generation, and text revision uses of AI, academic motivation, and perceived critical thinking dispositions.
summary.finding: Information retrieval use was positively associated with perceived critical thinking, content generation use was negatively associated, text revision use was not significant, and motivation moderated these associations.

papers.title: AI safety evaluation in an underrepresented population: real-world performance of clinical decision support and frontier language models on Medicaid patient messaging triage
papers.authors: Sanjay Basu, Sadiq Patel, Parth Sheth, Bernardo Arevalo, Jeremy Schifberg, John Morgan, Rajaie Batniji
papers.journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

summary.goal: To compare the safety and performance of guardrailed decision-support systems and frontier language models for triaging Medicaid patient messages.
summary.methodology: The study retrospectively evaluated 2,000 messages from Medicaid patients across three states using physician adjudication and multiple machine-learning, rule-based, ensemble, cascade, and frontier-LLM configurations.
summary.finding: No configuration enabled sufficiently accurate physician-unassisted triage, but two clinician-review workflows met the prespecified sensitivity-floor target.

papers.title: AI for Understanding Subtext in Film and Drama
papers.authors: Yair Neuman

summary.goal: The book aims to develop a method for using large language models to uncover subtext in film and drama.
summary.methodology: It presents a structured third-mind hermeneutic approach involving the human reader, the text, and artificial intelligence, illustrated through film and drama case studies.
summary.finding: The abstract states that this approach enriches aesthetic experience and sharpens interpretive skill.

papers.title: AI ethics after generative AI: from consequences to effects
papers.authors: Robert Gianni

summary.goal: The paper examines how repeated human–LLM interactions produce both identifiable consequences and cumulative effects on inquiry, self-understanding, and cultural meaning-making.
summary.methodology: It uses John Dewey’s pragmatist account of inquiry, habit formation, and moral reconstruction to develop a conceptual distinction between consequences and effects.
summary.finding: The paper argues that attending to cumulative effects complements existing AI ethics by addressing transformations emerging through everyday LLM use.

papers.title: AI chatbots and youth suicide risk: current evidence, critical gaps, and a clinical research agenda
papers.authors: Kelly L. Zuromski, Margaret Meagher, Tracy Costigan, Elizabeth A. Olson

summary.goal: The paper reviews evidence on how generative AI chatbots detect and respond to youth suicide risk and proposes a clinical research agenda.
summary.methodology: It synthesizes existing studies of general-purpose chatbots and AI companions, focusing on their responses to suicide-risk disclosures, and outlines qualitative, evaluative, and prospective research priorities.
summary.finding: Existing studies predominantly use single-turn researcher-generated prompts, chatbot performance declines with indirect or gradually disclosed risk, and real-world effects on youth suicide risk remain unknown.

papers.title: AI Tools and Writing Identity in EFL Contexts: A Mixed-Methods Study of Voice, Ownership, and Cultural Authenticity
papers.authors: Manel Mizab
papers.journal: International Journal of Current Educational Studies

summary.goal: The study investigates whether Algerian university students perceive reduced authenticity, voice, identity, and ownership in AI-assisted second-language writing.
summary.methodology: It uses a mixed-methods design with questionnaires and thematic analysis of responses from 20 first-year English students.
summary.finding: Students report reduced anxiety and improved grammatical accuracy but express ambivalence about authorship and often re-edit AI outputs to restore their personal style.

papers.title: AI Sycophancy Reverse-Utilization Theory (AI-SRUT) A Methodological Framework for Theoretical Self-Falsification via Inverted Satisfaction Engineering AI谄媚机制反向利用理论(AI-SRUT) 基于倒置满意度工程的理论自证伪方法论框架
papers.authors: He
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper proposes using LLM sycophancy as a tool for critically testing and falsifying humanities and social-science theories.
summary.methodology: It develops a framework that redirects model satisfaction toward rigorous critique and uses cross-model adversarial interactions for theoretical stress-testing.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: A self-training framework using pre-trained language models to detect and classify technology adoption in protest event analysis
papers.authors: Jun Liu, Xin Li

summary.goal: The paper aims to detect and classify technology adoption and contextual dynamics in protest events from large-scale news data.
summary.methodology: It develops a self-training pipeline combining pre-trained language models, syntactic graph convolutional networks, and pattern matching to reconstruct protest datasets while reducing manual annotation.
summary.finding: The framework supports context-sensitive protest event classification and demonstrates the analytical value of integrating LLMs with GCNs.

papers.title: A hybrid intelligence approach to qualitative data analysis combining manual and AI coding with mixed methods analyses of reliability and validity
papers.authors: Julia Boettinger, Christal Bürgel, Anne Bartsch

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether AI coding can complement or replace manual qualitative data analysis.
summary.methodology: Researchers compared manual coding of 164 interviews with AI coding under two prompting conditions and assessed reliability and validity using mixed quantitative and qualitative analyses.
summary.finding: AI identified many relevant segments and some missed by manual coding but substantially overcoded, so the authors recommend hybrid coding rather than replacing manual analysis.

papers.title: A Twelve-Layer Empirical Atlas of Terms and Phenomena from a Longitudinal Human-AI Interaction Corpus
papers.authors: Andreas Ehstand
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The study aims to create a machine-readable atlas of terms and phenomena from a longitudinal human–AI interaction corpus without releasing raw dialogues.
summary.methodology: It analyzes an N=1 corpus subset of 20,448 conversational turns involving two frontier language models and organizes 142,773 entries into twelve layers and three tiers.
summary.finding: The resulting atlas contains 23,911 empirical, 117,276 theoretical, and 1,586 methodological entries, while the underlying corpus and construction procedure remain restricted.

papers.title: A Study on the Impact of Generative AI on Consumer Decision-Making in Live-Streamed E-commerce within the Apparel Industry
papers.authors: yi jiang, Xueyu Zhao
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Economic Dynamics (JFED)

summary.goal: The study examines how virtual try-on tools, smart shopping assistants, and virtual hosts affect consumer decision-making in apparel livestreaming.
summary.methodology: It combines a literature review, case study, questionnaire survey, reliability and validity tests, correlation analysis, and Bootstrap mediation tests using the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework.
summary.finding: All three AI functions positively affect consumer decision-making, with smart shopping assistants having the strongest effect and perceived trust partially mediating all pathways.

papers.title: A Study of the Challenges and Professional Development Strategies for Foreign Language Teachers in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Ting Yang
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Science Education and Humanities

summary.goal: The study examines challenges faced by foreign language teachers and strategies for professional development in the context of AI-driven educational change.
summary.methodology: It uses the TPACK framework and Teacher Identity Theory to analyze AI’s impact on teachers’ professional development and identify pathways for sustainable growth.
summary.finding: The study argues that teachers should improve their knowledge, digital integration, teaching innovation, role adaptation, and lifelong learning, supported by institutional mechanisms.

papers.title: A Scoping Review of Generative AI Usage and Human Cognition in Education and Professional Practice: Dual-Edged Cognitive Impacts and a Governance Framework
papers.authors: Kaneeka Vidanage, Manith Marapperuma, Shakya Dissanayake, Faiz Mohideen Mohamed Thassim Marikar

summary.goal: The review examines how generative AI affects human cognition across education and professional practice and develops governance frameworks for responsible adoption.
summary.methodology: The authors conducted a PRISMA-ScR and JBI-guided scoping review of 107 peer-reviewed English-language publications from 2020–2025 identified across five databases.
summary.finding: The synthesis proposes a Cognitive Impact Taxonomy and an Integrated Cognitive Symbiosis Framework to maximize cognitive benefits while mitigating risks to critical thinking, creativity, and independent reasoning.

papers.title: A Hybrid Edge-AI Solution Combining Large Language Models and Computer Vision for Enhancing AgTech Access Among Indian Smallholder Farmers
papers.authors: Padma Mishra, Kinjal Doshi, Dr Shveti Chandan, Akanksha Kulkarni, Jala Prasadarao, Pavithra Shetty, Aseel Smerat
papers.journal: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Technology

summary.goal: The paper aims to improve localized agricultural advisory access for Indian smallholder farmers using an edge-deployed multimodal LLM system.
summary.methodology: It develops and field-evaluates AgriLLM-X, combining multilingual voice dialogue, computer vision, sensor fusion, genomic analysis, and edge optimization.
summary.finding: The system achieved high technical performance, increased reported agricultural yields by 15–22%, increased access for female farmers by 36%, and produced 91% user satisfaction.

papers.title: A Blinded Multi-LLM Content-Coding Instrument: Protocol Specification and Inter-Coder Reliability Validation on an Organizational Corpus
papers.authors: Dmitry Zharnikov
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper aims to specify and validate a blinded multi-LLM instrument for organizational content coding.
summary.methodology: Several LLMs independently coded evidence dossiers under blinding, with logged model calls and majority-vote-or-flag adjudication on a 30-case organizational corpus.
summary.finding: The instrument achieved almost-perfect inter-coder agreement (Fleiss' κ = .838), while human-coding validation remains future work.

papers.title: <p>Sequencing Human-Artificial Intelligence Creative Writing Collaboration Affects Perceived Authorship</p>
papers.authors: Philipp Lizat, Patrick Jost, Daria Leus, Melani Da Cunha Alves, Laureen Vanessa Schmidt

summary.goal: The study examines how the sequencing of human and AI contributions affects perceived creativity, authorship, and satisfaction in creative writing.
summary.methodology: In a between-subjects experiment with 84 participants, one group wrote a story before using generatestory.io to improve it, while another revised an AI-generated draft.
summary.finding: Participants reported similar satisfaction, but writing first increased initial authorship feelings, which became more similar after revision; early perceived authorship mediated later satisfaction, whereas perceived creativity did not.

papers.title: <b>An AI Enabled Comparison CDA Using ChatGPT and DeepSeek to Identify Discourse Strategies in Imam Ali’s Al-Shaqshaqiyya Sermon in Nahj al-Balagh</b>
papers.authors: Basim Badar, Muayyed Juma, Muna Abdualhussein Swear

summary.goal: The study aims to compare AI-enabled critical discourse analyses of Imam Ali’s Al-Shaqshaqiyya sermon.
summary.methodology: It applies the van Dijk, Fairclough, and Wodak models to the original Arabic sermon and its English translation using ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-3.5, and DeepSeek.
summary.finding: ChatGPT-4 provides the most accurate and consistent analysis, DeepSeek handles culturally and historically loaded Arabic elements well but is weaker with English, and English translations are more accessible but lose rhetorical force and cultural precision.

papers.title: <b>AI-Assisted Multilingual Pedagogy in Computing Education: A Culturo-Techno-Contextual Approach Framework for Enhancing Achievement and Attitudinal Outcomes in Mobile and Adaptive Systems</b><b></b>
papers.authors: Alli Abdurrazaq, Omar Camara, Saidu Conteh, Ebrima Kanteh

summary.goal: The study evaluated how traditional lectures and three AI-supported multilingual CTCA 2.0 instructional modalities affect students’ OSI model achievement and attitudes.
summary.methodology: A quasi-experimental study assigned 75 students in four intact groups and analyzed pre-test and post-test data using MANCOVA.
summary.finding: CTCA modalities produced significantly more positive attitudes, while their higher achievement means were not statistically significant compared with the control group.

papers.title: "Critical Language Ecosystem": About Truth, Power, and Digital Media from a Marxist Critical Philosophy Approach
papers.authors: Pham Tran Quynh, Nguyen Khanh Hung, Trần Nhật Minh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper develops a Marxist framework for analyzing how digital media and generative AI shape the relationship between linguistic truth and falsehood.
summary.methodology: It draws on modern language theories and Marxist theories of language, social consciousness, and alienation to analyze the formation and amplification of truth and falsehood.
summary.finding: The paper argues that a critical language ecosystem could help restore language’s truth-conveying function and foster a more humane and honest digital language culture.
